rules.title: Declare strict_types=1 in every namespaced PHP file

gate.id: [BE-001] every namespaced PHP file declares strict types

rules.summary: Every file in the application and database namespaces declares strict_types=1, checked by a Pest architecture test, and Pint's declare_strict_types fixer adds the declaration to route and config files as well.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: brownfield files get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink and the Pint fixer runs on changed files, never a mass rewrite, because strict types turn scalar coercion into type errors.

rules.title: Format PHP with Pint against a committed configuration that names its preset
rules.summary: A committed pint.json names the laravel preset plus individually justified rules, pint --test runs as its own check step, and the edit hook and pre-commit format changed files automatically.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt runs Pint once over the project and commits the result before the check is enabled.

rules.title: Pass Larastan at the project's level, with every parameter, return and property typed
rules.summary: phpstan analyse with the Larastan extension passes at the project's level (8 for greenfield projects, at least 6 for brownfield ones), so a missing type fails the run and existing errors live only in the shrink-only baseline.
rules.adoption: Baseline: brownfield projects start at level 6 with existing errors recorded in phpstan-baseline.neon.

rules.title: Keep the effective Larastan level, analysed paths and unmatched-ignore reporting at the floor
evasions: PHPStan run outside the composer analyse script, such as directly in a CI step or git hook, with a lower level or another configuration
a wrapper script the analyse script calls, whose flags the check does not read
rules.summary: The check reads the merged parameters and the composer analyse script, and fails when the level is below the floor for the project type, app, database, routes or tests is not analysed, an exclusion has no dated allowlist entry, reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors is off, or the script passes --level, -l, -c, --configuration or narrowed paths.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes the floor for the project type and keeps an existing configuration that is stricter.

rules.title: Never let the PHPStan baseline grow
evasions: a change pushed without a pull request, where no base-branch comparison runs
an existing ignoreErrors pattern broad enough to absorb a new error with the same message
rules.summary: The check counts every baseline entry, failing on one without a count, every ignoreErrors entry in the effective configuration and every inline ignore, and fails when the total exceeds the base branch's in pull-request CI; the sanctioned baseline:update script regenerates the baseline and fails if the total grew.
rules.adoption: Baseline: adopt generates the baseline with --allow-empty-baseline, and only baseline:update rewrites it afterwards.

rules.title: Never lower the PHPStan level, and raise it by the recorded due date
evasions: a level raise paid for with new ignoreErrors patterns instead of fixes
a due date moved through an allowlist entry whose reason is boilerplate
rules.summary: The check compares the effective level with the base branch and fails on any decrease, and once the recorded next-raise date has passed it fails unless the level went up or a dated allowlist entry with a reason moved the date; it also reports how many errors the next level would add.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt records the level at adoption as the starting point and a first due date one quarter ahead.

rules.title: Pass the Pest php preset: no debug, diagnostic or raw output calls such as var_dump, dump or echo

gate.id: [BE-007] php preset: no debug or diagnostic output

evasions: a banned function called dynamically, through call_user_func() or a variable function
output written through error_log() or fwrite() to a standard stream
rules.summary: The Pest php preset runs under an architecture test named with this rule's ID and fails on any name-resolved use of the debug, diagnostic and output functions it lists, across every non-test namespace including factories and seeders.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: the kit ships a dated ->ignoring() list for console commands and seeders that print output.

rules.title: Leave no untracked TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX marker: each one carries a ticket reference
evasions: synonyms outside the marker list, such as TBD or LATER
a reference that matches the pattern but names no real ticket
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule checks every comment, case-insensitively, and fails on a marker that does not match the configured ticket pattern, for example TODO(ABC-123):, while existing markers start in the baseline.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing untracked markers go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Commit no commented-out PHP code
evasions: commented fragments that do not parse as complete statements
code pasted into docblock prose
rules.summary: A heuristic custom PHPStan rule fails on comments whose body parses as PHP statements, docblock prose excluded, and existing findings start in the baseline.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Document in .env.example every env() key that project config files read
evasions: keys built from variables or constants are not seen
a project file classified as framework-known is not checked
rules.summary: The check walks config/ recursively, classifies each file as project or framework-known, and fails when a literal env() or Env::get() key read by a project file is missing from .env.example, where a commented key counts as documented.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt classifies the existing config files and appends the missing keys to .env.example.

rules.title: Run the test suite against uncached configuration

gate.id: [BE-011] the test suite runs against uncached configuration

rules.summary: A test asserts that the configuration is not cached when the suite runs, so a cached config file can never override the values pinned in phpunit.xml, however the runner is invoked.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit's phpunit.xml and test bootstrap never cache configuration.

rules.title: Pin a hermetic test environment in phpunit.xml with force="true"

gate.id: [BE-012] phpunit.xml pins a hermetic test environment

evasions: a key that affects requests or tenancy but is missing from the configured list stays unpinned
rules.summary: A test parses phpunit.xml and fails unless each configured environment key (by default an in-memory SQLite database, array cache, session and mail drivers and the sync queue) has its configured value and force="true".
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt merges the pinned entries into the existing phpunit.xml.

rules.title: Meet the configured backend test-coverage floor
evasions: coverage exclusions in the phpunit.xml source element or ignore annotations in code
tests that execute lines without asserting on their results
rules.summary: A local test:coverage script runs pest --coverage --min=<floor> (PCOV in CI, Xdebug documented) as its own CI step, with the floor measured at adoption and only ever raised.
rules.adoption: Baseline: the floor starts at the coverage measured at adoption and ratchets up; doctor reports a missing coverage driver.

rules.title: Add no new PHP copy-paste clones beyond the committed jscpd baseline
evasions: near-duplicates below the minimum clone size
clones with renamed identifiers or reordered statements
rules.summary: jscpd runs over the PHP sources with the committed baseline and --fail-on-new-clones instead of a global percentage threshold, so a new clone fails even when nobody regenerates the baseline; PROC-034 keeps the baseline itself shrink-only.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing clones go into the committed jscpd baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Serve every API route under a version prefix

gate.id: [BE-015] every API route is served under the version prefix

rules.summary: A route-table test fails when a route in the api middleware group does not match the configured version pattern (api/v<n>/ by default); the greenfield template enables it, and a live unversioned API records the exception instead.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default so a live unversioned API is not broken; the greenfield template enables it.

rules.title: Shape API URIs as kebab-case plural resources, with state transitions as POST sub-resource verbs

gate.id: [BE-016] API URIs are kebab-case plural resources

evasions: the plural check is a heuristic, so irregular plurals rely on allowlist entries
a state transition written as a PATCH of a status field on the resource
rules.summary: A route-table test checks that static URI segments are kebab-case plurals and that non-resourceful actions are POST {resources}/{id}/{verb} routes served by invokable controllers.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default; irregular plurals and existing URIs go into dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Route every request to a controller action; no route closures

gate.id: [BE-017] every route resolves to a controller action

rules.summary: A route-table test fails when an application route's action is a closure, with framework-registered routes such as the health route excluded by their source.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt replaces the framework's stub closures (the welcome page and the user route added by the API installer) with controller actions.

rules.title: Type the input of every POST, PUT and PATCH action as a FormRequest

gate.id: [BE-018] every write action takes a FormRequest

rules.summary: Reflection over the route table fails when a POST, PUT or PATCH action has no parameter typed as a FormRequest subclass, and a body-less write needs a dated allowlist entry.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Keep validation in FormRequests; no inline validation in the HTTP layer
rules.summary: A type-aware custom PHPStan rule fails on validator(), the Validator facade, the validation factory's make() and the request's validate() methods anywhere in App\Http outside FormRequest classes.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Name store and update requests Store{Model}Request and Update{Model}Request
evasions: a controller whose name does not reveal its model, so the expected request name cannot be derived
store and update methods outside resource controllers are not checked
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule checks the FormRequest parameter of store() and update() on resource controllers against the model name derived from the controller name.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Authorize each endpoint at exactly one site with exactly one policy ability

gate.id: [BE-021] each endpoint authorizes once with one ability

evasions: authorization performed inside a service the action calls
ability names built at run time
rules.summary: A meta-test over the route table fails when an action with a non-trivial FormRequest authorize() also authorizes in the controller, or when an endpoint references more than one ability.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Exercise every API route in at least one feature test

gate.id: [BE-022] every API route is exercised by a feature test

evasions: a trivial request that asserts nothing still counts as coverage
rules.summary: A listener records every route matched while the feature suite runs, and a final assertion fails for any registered API route that was never matched.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: untested routes at adoption go into a dated allowlist that only shrinks.

rules.title: Answer failed logins with one generic problem detail

gate.id: [BE-023] failed logins return one generic problem detail

rules.summary: A contract test sends an unknown account and a wrong password to the login route and fails unless both return the same status and the same body, problem details when the api-contract module is on, so responses never reveal which accounts exist.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit's login response already answers both failures the same way.

rules.title: Declare an allowed response type as the return type of every controller action

gate.id: [BE-024] every controller action declares an allowed response type

rules.summary: Reflection over public controller actions fails when the declared return type is missing or outside the configured set of Resources, resource collections and response classes, and Larastan then proves each return matches it.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Build JSON responses only through the sanctioned response path; never hand-roll them
rules.summary: A type-aware custom PHPStan rule fails on the response() helper, the Response facade, the response factory and direct JsonResponse construction outside the configured response emitter and the exception renderer.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Emit the configured success shape exactly: no ad-hoc top-level keys and no double data wrapping

gate.id: [BE-026] every JSON success response matches the configured shape

evasions: responses that no feature test exercises
rules.summary: A listener checks every 2xx JSON body in the feature suite against the configured shape (resource or envelope), including links and meta on paginated bodies, no data.data nesting and deletes per shape, with binary responses exempt.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the shape defaults to resource, and a project that already answers with an envelope sets modules.api-contract.shape to envelope.

rules.title: Render every API exception as RFC 9457 problem details from one renderer, with errors on 422

gate.id: [BE-027] every API exception renders as problem details

evasions: controllers or middleware that build their own error bodies
routes outside the renderer's API predicate
rules.summary: A test raises each mapped exception (validation, authentication, authorization, not found, method, throttle, HTTP and generic) through a route the renderer's API predicate covers and asserts application/problem+json with type, title and status, the right status code, and the field-to-messages map in errors on 422.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: an existing API scopes the renderer to a new version prefix (rules.BE-027.pathPrefix) or keeps legacy routes on their old error body through dated entries, because problem+json changes what shipped clients read.

rules.title: Use the status vocabulary: 409 for state and concurrency conflicts, 422 only for validation
rules.summary: Reviewers check that abort() and exception status choices follow the vocabulary (409 for conflicts, 422 for validation, 400 for unknown filter or sort keys, 429 for rate limits), each mapped to a problem type.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Never service-locate outside service providers: no app(), resolve(), App::make or container calls
evasions: app() or resolve() invoked dynamically, through call_user_func() or a variable function
rules.summary: An architecture test bans app(), resolve() and the App facade, container and application classes everywhere in App except App\Providers, resolved by name from the AST.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Add no pass-through layers: single-step CRUD and list queries stay in the controller
rules.summary: Reviewers reject per-entity services, query classes and empty stub layers, keeping single-step reads and writes inline in thin controllers.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Add a service only for a domain rule used outside HTTP; make shared multi-step writes Actions
rules.summary: Reviewers check each new service against the boundary: state machines, scoring and external rendering are services, multi-step writes reused across entry points are Actions, and a one-caller abstraction is inlined.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Add no repository or speculative layer classes (Repository, Manager, Handler, UseCase, Interactor)

gate.id: [BE-032] no repository or speculative layer classes

evasions: synonym suffixes outside the configured list, such as Store, Gateway, Dao or Processor
rules.summary: An architecture test bans the configured speculative suffixes across App, framework-shaped classes excepted, and fails when an App\Repositories namespace exists.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Implement every Action as an invokable class in App\Actions
rules.summary: An architecture test fails when a class in App\Actions is not invokable, so multi-step writes shared by controllers, jobs and commands use one Action shape that takes validated arrays or DTOs.
rules.adoption: Fix first: an existing App\Actions class without __invoke gains one before the check is enabled.

rules.title: Keep raw SQL, the DB facade and transactions out of the HTTP layer
rules.summary: A type-aware custom PHPStan rule fails on DB facade calls, database connection methods (transactions included) and raw query-builder methods anywhere in App\Http, so raw SQL lives in model scopes and transactions in services or Actions.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Keep services plain classes with no interface and no base class
rules.summary: An architecture test fails when a class in App\Services extends a class or implements an interface.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Place each kind of class in the namespace the configured placement map assigns it
rules.summary: A configurable namespace-to-kind map expands into architecture expectations in both directions, for example traits in Concerns, Scope implementations in App\Models\Scopes and ShouldQueue only in jobs, listeners, mail and notifications.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Pass the Pest laravel preset: framework class conventions and no env() outside config
evasions: a banned function called dynamically, through call_user_func() or a variable function
rules.summary: The Pest laravel preset runs under an architecture test named with this rule's ID, keeps enums in App\Enums, class suffixes and base classes, resourceful-only controller methods and queued mailables and jobs, and bans env() outside config; the debug functions it also bans are BE-007's property.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: the kit ships a dated ->ignoring() list, one rule ID per entry, for stock and kit code the preset rejects.

rules.title: Promote and mark readonly every constructor parameter of controllers, services and Actions

gate.id: [BE-038] collaborators are promoted readonly constructor parameters

rules.summary: Reflection over controllers, services and Actions fails when a constructor parameter is not promoted or not readonly; a collaborator created with new inside a method is a review item.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default.

rules.title: Keep controllers under the configured line count

gate.id: [BE-039] controllers stay under the line limit

rules.summary: An architecture test fails when a class in App\Http\Controllers, controller concerns included, reaches the configured line count.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Keep HTTP, validation and response concerns out of models
rules.summary: An architecture test fails when a class in App\Models uses the request, response, validator, auth or session helpers or their facades and classes.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Declare casts in the casts() method, not the $casts property
rules.summary: Reflection over App\Models fails when a model declares its own $casts property.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default.

rules.title: Name database columns in snake_case
rules.summary: A test reads the migrated schema and fails when a column name is not snake_case, with pre-existing tables in dated allowlist entries.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default; pre-existing tables go into dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Cast every status, state, type and role column to a string-backed enum

gate.id: [BE-043] status-like columns are cast to string-backed enums

evasions: status-like columns named outside the configured list, such as kind or phase
rules.summary: A test reads the migrated schema and fails when a column matching the configured names is not cast to a backed enum in its model's casts().
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Make every enum a native string-backed enum
rules.summary: An architecture test fails when an enum in App\Enums is not string-backed, and the laravel preset keeps every enum in that namespace.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Name enum cases in the configured style with snake_case backing values

gate.id: [BE-045] enum cases follow the naming style

rules.summary: Reflection over App\Enums fails when a case name breaks the configured style or a backing value is not snake_case.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default.

rules.title: Never compare enum-cast attributes to string literals; use the enum
evasions: string values held in variables or constants
raw SQL fragments and query scopes that take plain strings
rules.summary: A type-aware custom PHPStan rule fails when a where-style query argument or a strict comparison on an attribute that the model casts to a backed enum is a string literal.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Keep presentation data such as colors off enums; the API emits semantic state only
evasions: presentation methods outside the configured list, such as colour, hex or tone
color values emitted directly from Resources
rules.summary: An architecture test fails when an enum declares a method from the configured presentation list (color() by default), so clients map state to design tokens.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated ->ignoring() entries that only shrink.

rules.title: Emit enum values only; never add *_label display fields to Resources
evasions: display keys that do not end in _label, such as status_display
output keys built at run time
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule fails on literal output keys ending in _label in a Resource's toArray(), because clients render labels from their own message files.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Serialize models only through API Resources in the HTTP layer
rules.summary: A type-aware custom PHPStan rule fails on toArray(), toJson(), jsonSerialize(), attribute dumps, json_encode() and array casts of models or Eloquent collections anywhere in App\Http outside App\Http\Resources.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Define each wire shape once: one Resource per shape, summary Resources for nested relations
rules.summary: Reviewers reject inline {id, name} relation maps and duplicate shapes, and composite payloads get their own Resource.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Decide single-record access in policies and list visibility in a scope that mirrors them
rules.summary: Reviewers check that each policy and its visibility scope cross-reference each other and that policies do no list filtering.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Generate sequential codes with a database sequence or retry on unique violation, never max + 1
rules.summary: Reviewers check every code-generation path for race safety, because reading the current maximum and adding one issues duplicates under concurrency.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Enable Eloquent strict mode outside production

gate.id: [BE-053] Eloquent strict mode is on outside production

rules.summary: A test asserts that lazy loading, silently discarded attributes and missing-attribute access fail in the testing environment, so N+1 relation loads fail the suite.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default until existing lazy loads are fixed.

rules.title: Paginate every list (index) route
evasions: list actions not named index
index routes whose parameters the test dataset cannot build are skipped
rules.summary: A behavioural route-table test calls each GET index route as the configured actor and fails unless the body has the paginator shape with a server total.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Sanitize and hard-cap per_page, falling back to the default on invalid input
evasions: paginated routes the test dataset cannot call
rules.summary: A behavioural test calls each paginated route with negative, non-numeric and oversized per_page values and fails unless it answers 200 with a page size within the cap.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Accept only declared filter and sort keys; reject unknown keys with 400

gate.id: [BE-056] unknown filter and sort keys are rejected

evasions: list routes the test dataset cannot call
unknown keys under a parameter name the test does not probe
rules.summary: A behavioural test sends an unknown filter key and an unknown sort key to each list route and fails unless both answer 400, with the installed query-builder package as the preferred mechanism.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default.

rules.title: Use one filter idiom per project for list queries
rules.summary: Reviewers check that new list actions use the project's declared idiom: the installed query-builder package, or otherwise the when() chain.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Set server-derived fields in prepareForValidation(), never from client input
rules.summary: Reviewers check that owner, actor and other derived fields are pinned server-side in the FormRequest rather than accepted from the request body.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Keep wire field names equal to storage column names
rules.summary: Reviewers reject aliasing in validated() output and Resources; an unavoidable alias is applied in both the Store and Update requests and emitted from a real source.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Keep FormRequest messages() keys matched to rules that exist
evasions: rules() that depend on route parameters or request state cannot be evaluated
rules.summary: A reflection test instantiates each FormRequest and fails when a messages() key (attribute.rule) has no matching rule in rules().
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing violations get dated entries in the rule's allowlist file, which only shrink.

rules.title: Run the server-owned-field strip middleware first in the resolved API middleware stack

gate.id: [BE-061] the strip middleware runs first on every API route

rules.summary: A test resolves the HTTP kernel, gathers the global and route middleware of every api route (asserting the route set is not empty) and fails unless the strip middleware is present and runs before route-model binding.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Apply the active-tenant middleware to every authenticated API route

gate.id: [BE-062] every authenticated API route checks the active tenant

rules.summary: A test over the resolved middleware stack of every api route fails when a route that gathers an auth guard does not also gather the active-tenant middleware, with exceptions only as dated allowlist entries.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module; existing exceptions go into dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Wire tenancy into the user model only through the shipped traits; never redefine the tenant relation

gate.id: [BE-063] the user model wires tenancy through the shipped traits

rules.summary: Reflection over the configured user model fails unless tenant() and the tenancy predicates exist and are declared by the shipped scope and predicate traits.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Migrate the tenancy schema: a tenants table with non-null feature flags and tenant columns on users
rules.summary: A schema test fails unless the tenants table exists with a non-null, defaulted feature column and the user table carries the configured tenant, sub-tenant and operator columns, because otherwise every schema-driven tenancy gate passes vacuously.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Seed a valid tenancy state: an operator, the default tenant and no rows without a tenant

gate.id: [BE-065] seeding leaves a valid tenancy state

evasions: rows created outside the default seeder chain
rules.summary: A test runs the default seeder chain and fails unless an operator satisfies the bypass predicate, the configured default tenant exists and no tenant table holds a row without a tenant, operators excepted.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Build isolation-test fixtures from scratch; never depend on seeded tenants

gate.id: [BE-066] isolation tests build their own fixtures

evasions: seeding through a shared base test case or helper outside the scanned files
rules.summary: A token scan of the isolation test files fails on seeder calls, seed properties and reads of the default-tenant configuration.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Ship the tenant-isolation suites complete, with no todo, skipped or incomplete test
evasions: a mandated test edited to assert nothing meaningful
a skip or early return hidden in a helper outside the scanned suite files
rules.summary: The check asserts that every mandated isolation test name exists and reads PHP tokens, ignoring comments and strings, to fail on ->todo(, ->skip(, markTestIncomplete( and markTestSkipped( in those suites, with waivers only as dated allowlist entries.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module; the suites ship complete and run against the kit's plumbing.

rules.title: Scope list endpoints silently to the caller's tenant: foreign rows absent and totals tenant-only

gate.id: [BE-068] list endpoints are scoped to the caller tenant

evasions: totals computed by a separate unscoped count path the dataset does not exercise
rules.summary: A dataset-driven isolation test calls the index route of every tenant model as a user of another tenant and fails unless it answers 200 with no foreign rows and a total that counts only the caller's rows.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Apply the sub-tenant scope in every listing over a sub-tenant model

gate.id: [BE-069] sub-tenant listings apply the sub-tenant scope

evasions: sibling rows reached through eager-loaded relations
listings served outside index routes
rules.summary: A dataset-driven isolation test fails when a sub-tenant-restricted user listing a sub-tenant model sees rows of another sub-tenant.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Apply sub-tenant scoping only through the model-attached scope
evasions: a controller helper method that wraps the sub-tenant filter
rules.summary: An architecture test confines the sub-tenant trait to App\Models, and a token scan fails on hand-written sub-tenant where() clauses in controllers.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Block a disabled tenant at login and on existing tokens with one shared predicate and message

gate.id: [BE-071] suspending a tenant rejects new logins and requests with live tokens

evasions: a login flow that checks the tenant status column directly with its own message
rules.summary: A complete feature test disables a tenant and fails unless login and requests with existing tokens answer 403 with the shared message key and re-enabling restores both, and a token scan confirms the login flow calls the shared predicate.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Grant the platform bypass only to operators without a tenant, and honor it at every layer
evasions: a predicate override that drops the no-tenant condition on a path the tests do not exercise
rules.summary: A complete feature test fails unless an operator bound to a tenant never bypasses, the operator flag is cast to boolean, and a tenantless operator lists rows of two tenants and keeps access when a tenant is disabled.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Fail closed for a user without a resolvable tenant: no rows, no create and 403 on requests

gate.id: [BE-073] users without a resolvable tenant fail closed

evasions: a predicate override that treats a missing tenant row as active on a path the tests do not exercise
a query that drops the tenant scope with withoutGlobalScope()
rules.summary: Complete feature tests fail unless a non-bypassing user whose tenant is null or missing sees zero rows (never a whereNull match), fails the scoped exists rule, cannot create and gets 403, and an unassigned sub-tenant user sees an empty list.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: part of the tenancy module, installed with it as a complete unit.

rules.title: Name files and directories under the source root in kebab-case

evasions: fetch reached through computed or aliased globalThis access
a second client instance created inside the sanctioned module
rules.summary: A cross-stack/confine-api entry lets only the configured client module import the declared HTTP library and only the shared fetcher and the BFF forwarder call the global fetch, so every request goes through one client with the same headers, interceptors and error handling.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Keep the API version segment only in the upstream base URL
evasions: a version segment assembled at runtime from a variable or by concatenation
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: A global no-restricted-syntax selector flags string and template literals whose request path starts with a version segment matching the configured pattern, such as /v1/ or /api/v1/, so the API version changes in one base URL.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Poll live data through the server-state cache; import a realtime client only with a recorded ADR
evasions: the global WebSocket or EventSource, which needs no import
a realtime library the rule does not list
rules.summary: Live surfaces on web and mobile poll through the server-state cache, and a module-boundary lint rule reports static and dynamic imports of realtime client libraries unless the manifest's decisions section references an existing ADR.
rules.adoption: Fix first: an existing realtime client needs an ADR referenced from the manifest's decisions section.

rules.title: Log only through the logger module; no direct console calls
evasions: console reached through a globalThis or window member access
rules.summary: Core no-console plus no-restricted-globals on console, which also catches aliasing through a local binding, fail direct console use on web and mobile everywhere except the logger module.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Mint a request id when absent and forward it on every upstream call

gate.id: [WEB-041] the shared forwarder mints a missing request id and forwards it upstream

evasions: a second HTTP client or handler that bypasses the shared forwarder
rules.summary: With the observability module, the shared forwarder mints a request id when the incoming request has none, preserves an incoming one and sends it on every upstream call, so one id links browser, BFF and API logs.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: arrives with the observability module after 1.0 and is turned on through rules.WEB-041.enabled.

rules.title: Validate each field on the client in forms above the configured field count
rules.summary: Forms with more fields than the configured threshold, about five by default, validate each field on the client with the installed form and validation libraries as a UX aid, while the server stays the authority on validity.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Map server validation errors onto their fields and wire aria-invalid and aria-describedby
rules.summary: The errors member of a 422 problem response is mapped onto the matching form fields, each invalid field sets aria-invalid and references its message through aria-describedby, and the summary message is only the fallback.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: List every private route segment in the protected-segments declaration the proxy reads

gate.id: [WEB-044] every private route segment is listed in the protected-segments declaration

evasions: a private page placed outside the conventional protected route groups
the proxy no longer reading the exported list, which the test does not assert
proxy matcher exclusions such as paths containing a dot
rules.summary: A web architecture test imports the routes module, walks every route group under the app root and fails when the first URL segment of a non-public page is missing from the exported protected-segments list that drives the proxy's UX redirect.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the bff-auth module templates ship the routes module and the test.

rules.title: Reconcile the session hint with the token cookie in the proxy on every navigation

gate.id: [WEB-045] the proxy reconciles the session hint with the token cookie

evasions: an early return in the proxy before reconciliation runs
paths the proxy matcher excludes
rules.summary: The proxy compares the presence-only session hint cookie with the httpOnly token cookie on every navigation and corrects a drifted hint, so the client never believes it is signed in without a token, or signed out while holding one.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: shipped with the bff-auth module templates.

rules.title: Clear the profile cache and hard-navigate to the locale's login page on a non-login 401

gate.id: [WEB-046] a non-login 401 clears the profile cache and redirects to the login page

evasions: a second HTTP client without the unauthorized handler
rules.summary: The client's unauthorized handler treats a 401 from any endpoint except login as an expired session: it clears the persisted profile cache and navigates to the login page of the active locale, while a failed login shows its error in place.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: shipped with the bff-auth module templates.

rules.title: Compare auth endpoint paths as exact shared constants, never by substring
evasions: a regular-expression test on the path
an auth path held in a variable or built at runtime
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: Code that recognises auth endpoints compares against the declared auth-path constants exactly, and a global no-restricted-syntax selector flags includes, startsWith and endsWith calls on configured auth path literals, because substring matches misfire on similar paths.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Return RFC 9457 problem details for every error the BFF creates itself

gate.id: [WEB-048] errors the BFF fabricates are RFC 9457 problem details

evasions: a hand-built error response in a handler the tests do not exercise
rules.summary: Every error response the BFF creates locally, such as an unreachable upstream, a rejected path, a refused origin or a failed login or logout, is application/problem+json with type, title and status, matching the API's error format so clients parse one shape.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: shipped with the bff-auth module templates.

rules.title: Reject request bodies above the shared upload limit with 413 in the BFF, before buffering

gate.id: [WEB-049] the BFF rejects bodies over the upload limit with 413 before buffering

evasions: backend upload rules that read a different key or a literal
uploads sent directly to the API origin
rules.summary: The BFF reads the upload limit from the env key the backend upload rules also read and answers a larger body with 413 before buffering it or calling upstream, so an oversized upload cannot exhaust BFF memory.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: shipped with the bff-auth module templates.

rules.title: Cap block nesting depth
rules.summary: Core max-depth fails blocks nested deeper than the configured depth on web and mobile, with a lenient default so existing code mostly passes and the rest starts in bulk suppressions.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Cap function length
rules.summary: Core max-lines-per-function fails functions longer than the configured number of code lines on web and mobile, with a lenient default so existing code mostly passes and the rest starts in bulk suppressions.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Send credentials and the XSRF token from the SPA client, and fetch the CSRF cookie first

gate.id: [WEB-052] the SPA HTTP client sends credentials and the XSRF token

evasions: a second HTTP client or a direct fetch call that bypasses the shared client
a mutation on a code path the test does not exercise before the CSRF cookie is fetched
rules.summary: In the react-spa profile with cookie-based Sanctum SPA authentication, the shared HTTP client sends credentials and the X-XSRF-TOKEN header, fetches the CSRF cookie before the first state-changing request and never attaches a bearer token.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: arrives with the react-spa profile after 1.0 and is turned on through rules.WEB-052.enabled.

rules.title: Leave no untracked TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX marker in JavaScript or TypeScript
evasions: synonyms outside the marker list, such as TBD or LATER
a reference that matches the pattern but names no real ticket
rules.summary: The Standard's own cross-stack/no-untracked-todo rule reads every comment on web and mobile, case-insensitively, and fails on a marker without a ticket reference matching the configured pattern, for example TODO(ABC-123):, because core no-warning-comments cannot admit a referenced marker.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing untracked markers go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Keep top-level source folders within the configured folder contract
rules.summary: Every directory directly under the mobile source root is on the configured folder list, and platform or tooling directories are excluded only through a configurable ignore list, so the app layout cannot drift.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: the source root and folder list come from config and tsconfig, so both the src/app layout and the older root layout pass; extra folders get dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Default-export the screen or layout from every route file
rules.summary: Each file under the routes directory has a default export, because the file-based router renders only that export; API routes and native-intent files are exempt through a configurable file-name pattern.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Create React contexts only inside the contexts folder
rules.summary: createContext is reachable only from files in the configured contexts folder, whether it is imported by name or reached through the default React import, a namespace import or require, so every shared context has one home.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Keep only .ts files, never .tsx, in the utils, constants and types folders
rules.summary: A structure check fails on a .tsx file under the configured utils, constants and types folders, and because TypeScript rejects JSX syntax in .ts files, no JSX can live there.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing .tsx files in those folders get dated allowlist entries until they move.

rules.title: Define hooks only in the hooks and contexts folders
evasions: a hook function whose name does not start with use followed by a capital letter
rules.summary: A cross-stack/confine-api entry reports functions and variables named like a hook (use followed by a capital letter) declared outside the configured hooks and contexts folders, and the framework preset's rules-of-hooks check rejects hook calls inside functions not named like hooks.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Keep the types folder free of runtime code
rules.summary: The cross-stack/type-only-module rule, applied through a files override to the configured types folder and used by no other registry rule, reports top-level or exported variables, functions, classes, non-ambient enums and namespaces, default exports and expression statements there, so the folder holds only type-level declarations.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Place domain hooks and components in per-domain subfolders, with only cross-cutting ones at the root
evasions: domain code in a correctly named file inside another domain's folder
a domain file added to the configured cross-cutting list
rules.summary: Files directly under hooks and components must be on the configured cross-cutting list, and files under hooks/<domain>/ are named use followed by a capital letter, so each domain's code stays together.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default; the hooks and components roots follow the configured source root, and files still at a folder root get dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Import no server-state library in route files
rules.summary: Modules under the routes directory never import the server-state library, so data reaches routes only through screen hooks and route files stay thin.
rules.adoption: Baseline: dependency-cruiser known-violations, shrink-only under check-baselines:depcruise.

rules.title: Consume contexts only through their exported provider hook, which throws outside the provider
evasions: React 19 use(Context) called outside the contexts folder
a provider hook that returns a default value instead of throwing outside its provider
rules.summary: useContext is reachable only from the configured contexts folder, so consumers call each context's exported hook, and that hook throws when used outside its provider instead of returning a silent default.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Keep tracked file names identical in case to the files on disk
rules.summary: Every path git tracks matches its on-disk entry case-sensitively, and the check fails closed in CI when git is unavailable, so a case-only rename cannot break imports on case-sensitive build machines.
rules.adoption: Fix first: a git mv of each reported file fixes every finding at adoption.

rules.title: Import through the root path alias; no parent-relative imports
rules.summary: Static, dynamic and require imports whose relative path climbs out of the importing file's directory are reported, so cross-folder imports use the root alias read from tsconfig paths.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only; the alias comes from tsconfig paths, so both @/* to ./src/* and the older root layout work.

rules.title: Keep list page, filters and sort in navigation params and forward them to the API
rules.summary: A list screen keeps its page, filters and sort in navigation params, the mobile counterpart of URL state, and sends them to the API so the server's paging and totals drive the UI.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Keep server data only in the server-state cache: API access flows through query hooks
evasions: query data copied into component state or a store after it is fetched
server data persisted to device storage beyond the documented profile-cache exception
the global fetch() called directly when the HTTP library is the platform fetch
rules.summary: The HTTP library is reachable only from the API client module, and the API client module only from hooks and the auth context, so screens get server data through query hooks and the cache stays the single copy.
rules.adoption: Baseline: dependency-cruiser known-violations, shrink-only under check-baselines:depcruise.

rules.title: Create exactly one query client, in the query provider module
rules.summary: The server-state library's QueryClient constructor is reachable only from the configured query provider module and test utilities, so the app has a single cache with one set of defaults.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Show mutation feedback once, from the central mutation cache; opt out only with silent meta
evasions: mutation results reported through Alert or a hand-rolled notification component
a toast library that the configuration does not name
rules.summary: The configured toast library is reachable only from the query provider module and the toast host, so mutation feedback comes from the central mutation cache and a mutation opts out only through silent meta.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default; enable after mutation toasts move into the query provider, with known violations baselined shrink-only.

rules.title: Normalize API failures in one module; screens never read raw HTTP statuses or bodies
evasions: the status read through destructuring, such as const { status } = error.response
the error object passed to a helper that reads the response under another property path
rules.summary: A cross-stack/confine-api entry reports member chains that read .response.status or .response.data, with or without optional chaining, outside the configured error-normalizer module, so screens handle typed error kinds instead of raw responses.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Map every error response to a typed app-error kind per the configured format and statuses

gate.id: [MOB-017] maps each configured status and the 422 errors member to typed error kinds

evasions: a status the backend returns but the configured vocabulary omits
an error body in a format other than the configured one, such as an HTML page from a proxy
rules.summary: A table-driven contract test shipped with the error normalizer asserts that a response for each status in the configured vocabulary, 409 and 429 included, maps to its own kind, and that a 422 errors member maps to field errors.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit ships the normalizer with its test; a project keeping its own normalizer adapts it to the test table.

rules.title: Unwrap API responses in one typed function inside the API client; no .data.data downstream
evasions: nested destructuring such as const { data: { data } } = response
the inner payload read through an intermediate variable, such as const body = response.data; body.data
rules.summary: A cross-stack/confine-api entry reports member chains reading .data.data, in dot or computed-literal form, outside the API client module, so one typed unwrap function owns the success shape and callers never unwrap twice.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Take backend resource and enum types from the generated, committed API contract
evasions: a hand-written type whose name and member set both differ from the generated schema it mirrors
a mirror derived through mapped or utility types rather than a literal declaration
an inline object type or literal union used without a named declaration
rules.summary: A check flags type aliases, interfaces and string-literal unions whose name or member set matches a schema or enum in the generated contract, so the app uses generated types instead of hand-written mirrors that drift from the backend.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing hand-written mirrors get dated entries in .cross-stack/allowlists/MOB-019.json until they are replaced by generated types.

rules.title: Never narrow a value with a type assertion; rely on the generated types or a runtime parser
evasions: a user-defined type guard that always returns true
a value typed through a declaration file or overload that misstates its shape
rules.summary: Type assertions whose target type is narrower than the expression's type, double assertions through unknown included, are reported, so untrusted values are typed by the generated contract or validated by a runtime parser.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: off by default because brownfield code asserts widely; enable with ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only.

rules.title: Switch mock and live transport only inside the API client module
rules.summary: The env module's transport-mode exports are reachable only from the API client module, so hooks and screens run unchanged against the mock and the live backend.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: applies only to projects that use the mock transport.

rules.title: Reference public build-time variables statically; never read process.env with a computed key
evasions: destructuring process.env, which only the companion rule expo/no-env-var-destructuring reports
process.env assigned to another variable and indexed through it
rules.summary: Computed process.env reads are reported, because the bundler inlines only static process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_NAME accesses and a computed read is undefined in the built app.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Render the Redirect component only in route-group layouts and the entry route
evasions: a guard written as an imperative router.replace() inside a screen, which the rule does not see
rules.summary: The router's Redirect component is reachable only from _layout files and the configured entry route, so declarative guards and boot routing live in one place per route group.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Validate form fields on the client and map server field errors onto their fields
rules.summary: Forms with more than the configured number of fields validate each field on the client, and the server's 422 errors member is mapped onto the matching fields, with the summary message only as a last resort.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Never send, filter by or reason about the tenant id on the client
evasions: the tenant key built dynamically, such as with a template literal or string concatenation
tenant data read through a generic record accessor
the key spelled in a different case or form from the configured column
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: A global no-restricted-syntax selector reports identifiers, member properties and object or destructuring keys equal to the configured tenant key in mobile source, because the backend derives the tenant from the authenticated user and the client never supplies it.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Type-check every JavaScript track in TypeScript strict mode
evasions: source files left out of the checked tsconfig's include or files lists
a typecheck member that calls tsc through a wrapper script the sub-check does not follow
rules.summary: The resolved compiler options of each web and mobile tsconfig, extends chain included, set strict to true and switch off none of its member flags, the sub-check fails when the typecheck script runs tsc with -p or --project pointing at an unchecked tsconfig, and tsconfig files are gate-protected.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the Expo and Next.js templates already set strict: true; a project without it fixes the reported tsc errors before the check is enabled.

rules.title: Ban TypeScript suppression comments except a described @ts-expect-error
rules.summary: @ts-ignore and @ts-nocheck are reported and @ts-expect-error is allowed only with a description, so every silenced type error is visible, explained and flagged once it no longer applies.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing @ts-ignore comments become described @ts-expect-error comments or go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only.

rules.title: Let the HTTP client set the multipart content type and boundary; never set them by hand
evasions: the header value held in a variable or constant
the header set through a Headers instance or a set() call
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: A global no-restricted-syntax selector reports an object property keyed Content-Type, in any letter case, whose literal value starts with multipart/, because a hand-set header drops the boundary the HTTP client generates for a FormData body.
rules.adoption: Baseline: ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines:eslint-suppressions.

rules.title: Re-register the device push token when the active tenant changes
rules.summary: When the user switches the active tenant, the app registers its push token again for the new tenant, so notifications follow the current tenant and stop for the previous one.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess in the mobile tsconfig
rules.summary: When the rule is enabled, the resolved compiler options of the mobile tsconfig set noUncheckedIndexedAccess to true, so indexed reads are typed as possibly undefined.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: noUncheckedIndexedAccess yields many tsc errors on brownfield code and tsc has no baseline, so it stays off until the project enables it.

rules.title: Meet the configured mobile unit-test coverage floors
evasions: assertion-free tests that only execute lines
coverage exclusions and ignore comments
rules.summary: The mobile test:coverage run uses jest --coverage with collectCoverageFrom, so untested files count, and coverageThreshold floors that are measured at adoption and only move up.
rules.adoption: Baseline: floors start at the coverage measured at adoption and ratchet upward only.

rules.title: Leave no unused files, exports or dependencies on the mobile track
evasions: an export tagged @public, which knip does not report
modules reached only through dynamic imports knip cannot resolve
ignore entries added to the knip configuration
rules.summary: knip builds the module graph from the Expo entry points and fails on unused files, exports and dependencies, with existing findings held as dated allowlist entries that may only shrink.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: current knip findings are recorded as dated entries in .cross-stack/allowlists/MOB-032.json that may only shrink.

rules.title: Introduce no mobile copy-paste clones beyond the committed duplication baseline
evasions: clones shorter than the configured minimum lines or tokens
copies reworded or reordered until their tokens differ
rules.summary: jscpd runs over the mobile TypeScript sources with the committed baseline and --fail-on-new-clones, so any new clone fails while existing ones are paid down; PROC-034 keeps the baseline shrink-only.
rules.adoption: Baseline: the jscpd baseline is recorded at adoption and kept shrink-only by PROC-034.

rules.title: Call no insecure PHP functions such as eval, exec, md5, sha1, unserialize or rand

gate.id: [SEC-001] application code uses no insecure PHP functions

evasions: dynamic invocation through call_user_func or a variable function
the backtick shell operator
an insecure function missing from the preset list
rules.summary: The Pest security preset scans the application namespace for insecure functions such as eval, exec, shell_exec, system, md5, sha1, uniqid, rand, mt_rand, unserialize, extract and assert, with exceptions only through dated ->ignoring() allowlist entries.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: ship the exact ->ignoring() list (rand() in factories, echo in seeders and commands), each entry with the rule ID and an expiry date; brownfield hits get dated entries.

rules.title: Map GET and HEAD routes only to index, show or allowlisted read actions

gate.id: [SEC-002] GET and HEAD routes map only to read actions

evasions: a write performed inside an index or show action
rules.summary: A route-table test maps every GET and HEAD route to an index, show or allowlisted read-only action, because RFC 9110 defines both methods as safe and browsers, caches and crawlers send them without the user's intent, so a state-changing GET invites request forgery.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: ship the framework's GET email-verification route and any existing GET logout route as default entries with reasons, and check only application controller actions.

rules.title: Declare authorize() in every FormRequest and never return a constant true from it
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule fails a FormRequest that does not declare authorize(), which Laravel treats as authorized, and one whose inferred return type is the constant true (return true, return !false, return (bool) 1); a helper returning bool passes, so SEC-004's policy-ability meta-test does the real authorization check.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing hits go into the shrink-only PHPStan baseline; new requests cannot add one.

rules.title: Resolve every non-public route to an existing policy ability, and allowlist public routes

gate.id: [SEC-004] every non-public route resolves to an existing policy ability

evasions: a dynamic ability string
a Gate::define closure instead of a policy
authorize() called on a dead branch
Gate::allows() called with its result ignored
rules.summary: A policy-ability meta-test extracts the ability and model of every non-public route from its FormRequest, controller Gate calls, can middleware or attribute, and asserts that the model's policy defines that method; public routes come from a dated allowlist.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: adopt generates a dated entry (reason plus expiry) for each existing route without a policy, shares the public-route list with SEC-005 and never offers a silent skip.

rules.title: Require authentication on every non-public API route

gate.id: [SEC-005] every non-public API route requires authentication

rules.summary: A route-table test over the resolved middleware stack (global plus gathered route middleware, groups expanded, a non-empty route set asserted) requires the configured authentication middleware on every API route outside the public allowlist, and an unauthenticated request gets 401.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: the shipped default list holds the framework's public routes (health, sanctum/csrf-cookie, broadcasting/auth) so a fresh install passes; brownfield public routes get dated entries.

rules.title: Rate-limit every unauthenticated API route with a bounded limiter

gate.id: [SEC-006] every unauthenticated API route is rate-limited

evasions: a finite limit set so high that it never throttles
a limiter key callback that gives every request its own bucket
rules.summary: A route-table test over the resolved middleware stack requires a middleware derived from the framework's ThrottleRequests on every API route without authentication, resolves each named limiter through the RateLimiter and fails on Limit::none() or no limit, with exceptions only through dated allowlist entries.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: reads the same shipped public-route list as SEC-005, so the framework's own public routes do not fail a fresh install.

rules.title: Rate-limit every mutating authenticated API route with a bounded limiter

gate.id: [SEC-007] every mutating authenticated API route is rate-limited

evasions: a finite limit set so high that it never throttles
a limiter key callback that gives every request its own bucket
rules.summary: When enabled, the same resolved-stack test requires a throttle whose named limiter resolves to a finite limit on every authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE route; it is off by default because turning it on fails most existing projects at once.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: enable it once the API group carries a throttle, with dated allowlist entries for the remaining routes.

rules.title: Cap attempts per minute on the login, password change and password reset routes

gate.id: [SEC-008] credential routes cap attempts per minute

evasions: a credential route missing from the configured list
a limiter whose key or response callback weakens the cap
rules.summary: A test resolves the named limiters on the configured credential routes and asserts that their maximum attempts per minute are at or below the configured cap.
rules.adoption: Fix first: configure the credential routes at adoption and give any route on the generic API limiter a stricter named limiter.

rules.title: Return the access token at the documented response path from the token login route

gate.id: [SEC-009] login returns the access token at the documented path

rules.summary: When the API issues its own bearer tokens, declared by configuring the token login route, a contract test with factory data calls that route and asserts that the token sits at the configured path the BFF and the mobile client read; the test ships complete so it cannot pass while empty.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: turned on by declaring the token login route and token path at adoption to match the existing contract; an API that authenticates through cookie sessions, Passport or an external identity provider leaves them unset.

rules.title: Revoke the current access token on logout

gate.id: [SEC-010] logout revokes the current access token

rules.summary: When the API issues its own bearer tokens, declared by configuring the token login route, a contract test captures a token at login, calls the configured logout route and asserts that the same token then gets 401.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: applies once the token login route is declared (rules.SEC-009.loginRoute); a logout that only forgets the token on the client fails until it deletes the current token.

rules.title: Give access tokens a finite expiration at or below the configured bound

gate.id: [SEC-011] access tokens have a finite expiration

rules.summary: When the API issues its own bearer tokens, declared by configuring the token login route, a configuration test asserts that the token guard's expiration is set and at or below the configured upper bound, because a token issued without an expiration stays valid until someone revokes it.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: applies once the token login route is declared; an existing API whose tokens never expire records a dated allowlist entry until its token-strategy decision (SEC-055) sets a lifetime.

rules.title: Expose no exception message, class or trace in error responses when debug is off

gate.id: [SEC-012] error responses hide exception internals when debug is off

evasions: an HttpException message passed through verbatim
a custom exception handler that bypasses the central renderer
rules.summary: With debug off, a renderer test raises a generic exception through an API route and asserts a generic body with no exception message, class name or stack trace, in any response format, and with the api-contract module on also a problem-details response.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit's central renderer satisfies it; a project renderer that copies exception messages switches to generic details first.

rules.title: Persist only validated input in write actions, never raw request input
evasions: raw input read in a service and merged with validated()
query-string reads inside a write action
rules.summary: A type-aware PHPStan rule fails raw request accessors (all, input, only, except, post, json, collect and magic properties) inside controller write actions, so only validated() or safe() data reaches models.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing hits go into the shrink-only PHPStan baseline; new write actions must use validated() or safe().

rules.title: Pair a key-only guarded model with the strip middleware, creating hook and validated writes

gate.id: [SEC-014] a key-only guarded model has the strip middleware, creating hook and validated writes

evasions: a model that extends Model directly instead of the base model
rules.summary: When the configured base model guards only its key, a test asserts that the server-owned-field strip middleware is in the resolved API group, a creating hook stamps the configured server-owned fields from the authenticated context and the raw-input rule (SEC-013) is enabled, and with the tenancy module also that the hook refuses a foreign tenant id.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: a project whose models list their fillable attributes passes, and one that guards only the key gets the strip middleware and the creating hook from the kit.

rules.title: Apply the tenant scope to every model whose table has the tenant column, with no exceptions

gate.id: [SEC-015] every model whose table has the tenant column uses the tenant scope

rules.summary: A test walks the migrated schema, maps each table that carries the tenant column to its model and fails when that model lacks the configured tenant-scope trait; by design no allowlist or baseline can excuse a miss.
rules.adoption: Fix first: by design the tenancy module is adopted only once every tenant table's model carries the trait.

rules.title: Give every table the tenant column unless it is a declared global table

gate.id: [SEC-016] every non-global table has the tenant column

rules.summary: An inverse schema test fails any migrated table, uploads and device tokens included, that lacks the tenant column and is not in the declared global-table list.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt lists the existing shared tables as declared global tables for review.

rules.title: Scope every model with a sub-tenant column by the sub-tenant trait or a dated allowlist entry

gate.id: [SEC-017] every sub-tenant model is scoped or allowlisted

rules.summary: A schema-reading test requires every model whose table carries a configured sub-tenant column to use the sub-tenant trait or to appear in the allowlist with a reason and an expiry date.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: unscoped sub-tenant models get dated entries that name their controller-level mechanism.

rules.title: Cover every tenant-scoped model and tenant-aware job in the isolation suites

gate.id: [SEC-018] the isolation suites cover every tenant model and tenant-aware job

evasions: a dataset entry whose test asserts nothing meaningful
rules.summary: Set equality between the tenant models found in the migrated schema, the tenant-aware queued classes found by reflection and the datasets of the HTTP and background isolation suites fails when a subject is missing, and incomplete tests fail the run.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt seeds the dataset from the schema and reflection, so the suite starts complete.

rules.title: Validate foreign keys to tenant-scoped tables with the tenant-scoped exists rule

gate.id: [SEC-019] tenant foreign keys use the tenant-scoped exists rule

evasions: a table named through a variable
an exists rule applied in a controller or service
rules() that need route context to evaluate
rules.summary: A reflection test evaluates each FormRequest's rules(), splits pipe strings, resolves Rule::exists and class-string forms and fails on a plain exists against a tenant table, while the package suite proves the scoped rule returns 422 for a foreign id.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: requests whose rules() cannot be evaluated get dated entries until they are refactored.

rules.title: Pin the tenant or declare cross-tenant access with a reason in every background class

gate.id: [SEC-020] every background entrypoint pins the tenant or declares cross-tenant access

evasions: a queued closure, such as dispatch(function () {...}), a closure in Bus::chain or dispatchAfterResponse, which is not a class
a defer() callback
the marker is present but handle() drops the tenant scope with withoutGlobalScope()
rules.summary: Reflection over every concrete queued class (jobs, listeners, mailables, notifications), console command, scheduled event and controller behind an unauthenticated route requires the tenant-aware middleware or trait backed by TenantContext, or #[CrossTenant(reason: '...')]; a blank reason or a comment-only declaration fails.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt adds the tenant-aware middleware to existing queued classes or a #[CrossTenant] attribute with a reason; scheduled closures become jobs or commands.

rules.title: Answer cross-tenant direct access with 404, never 403
evasions: a route whose parameters the dataset cannot build
rules.summary: A dataset-driven isolation test calls the show, update and delete routes of every tenant model with another tenant's id and asserts 404, so a foreign record's existence is never confirmed.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the global tenant scope yields 404 before authorization; routes that load records without it are fixed.

rules.title: Give every upload rule a size cap and type and extension allowlists without script formats

gate.id: [SEC-022] every upload rule has a size cap and type allowlists

evasions: rules built at runtime or wrapped in custom rule objects
a type trusted from the client Content-Type header in a controller
rules.summary: Reflection over FormRequest rules() requires every file rule to carry max:, content-derived types (mimes or File::types) and extensions:, and rejects svg, image:allow_svg, html and xml.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: the reflection test has no native baseline, so adopt records existing upload requests as dated entries in .cross-stack/allowlists/SEC-022.json, which only shrink.

rules.title: Enforce the morph map so polymorphic parent types come from an explicit allowlist
rules.summary: A test asserts that Relation::requiresMorphMap() is on and that upload requests constrain the parent-type field with an In rule, so a client cannot name an arbitrary model class.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: enabling it needs a morph map that covers every existing polymorphic type, because an enforced map rejects unmapped classes.

rules.title: Authorize file access by ownership of the file or its parent record, never by login alone
rules.summary: Upload, download and delete abilities check that the caller owns the file or its parent record, which reviewers confirm in the file policies.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review against the file abilities in existing policies.

rules.title: Store uploads under the validated extension, never a name derived from the sniffed type
evasions: another storage write with a computed name, such as Storage::put() with hashName()
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule disallows UploadedFile::store(), storePublicly() and Storage::putFile() on uploads in favour of storeAs() with the validated extension, because a name derived from the sniffed type can turn an upload into an executable file.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing calls go into the shrink-only PHPStan baseline.

rules.title: Store attachment ids, never URLs, and serve private files through short-lived signed URLs
rules.summary: Columns, requests and responses carry attachment ids, and private files are reached only through signed URLs generated at read time with a short lifetime, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review; stored URLs are migrated to ids when the owning feature is next changed.

rules.title: Redact credentials and personal data in every log channel

gate.id: [SEC-027] every log channel carries the redaction processor

evasions: personal data under a key missing from the redaction list
rules.summary: The kit's log processor redacts the configured credential keys (authorization, token, password, cookie) and personal-data keys, and a test asserts that every configured log channel carries it.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt adds the processor to every configured channel.

rules.title: Keep the error tracker from sending personal data by default

gate.id: [SEC-028] error reporting sends no default personal data

rules.summary: With the observability module, a configuration test asserts that the error tracker's send-default-personal-data option is off; the rule stays off by default until the observability decision is accepted.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: arrives with the observability module after 1.0 and is turned on through rules.SEC-028.enabled.

rules.title: Put readiness checks and infrastructure detail behind operator authorization
rules.summary: The readiness route carries the operator ability and the public liveness route exposes no dependency or infrastructure detail, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review against the readiness route's ability.

rules.title: Make broadcast channels private and authorized, and tenant-scoped with the tenancy module
rules.summary: Once broadcasting is adopted by ADR, every channel is private with an authorization callback, and with the tenancy module each callback checks the tenant, which reviewers confirm in the channel definitions.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review against the channel authorization callbacks.

rules.title: Import server-only in every module under the configured server paths

gate.id: [SEC-031] every module under the server paths imports server-only

rules.summary: A web architecture test parses every module under the configured server paths and requires an import of server-only, so the framework build fails when client code reaches one.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt adds the import to existing modules under the server paths.

rules.title: Keep the upstream API base URL in server-side env, never in a public-prefixed variable
