gate.id: [SEC-032] the public env schema exposes no API base URL

evasions: a public variable whose name does not match the API pattern
a default API URL hardcoded in code
rules.summary: A test imports the typed env module and asserts that the API base URL key exists only in the server schema and that no public-prefixed key matching the API pattern exists in the schema or the example env file.
rules.adoption: Fix first: moving the variable to the server schema is part of adopting bff-auth.

rules.title: Limit the proxy session redirect to a cookie-presence check that never authorizes
rules.summary: The Next.js proxy only redirects signed-out visitors by cookie presence, while session validation and authorization happen in Route Handlers, Server Actions and the backend, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review; reviewers move any validation found in the proxy into the handlers.

rules.title: Re-verify the session in every Route Handler and Server Action, and authorize in the backend
evasions: the session helper is called but its result is ignored
the helper runs on only some code paths
the export is produced by a factory the rule does not know
a Server Component fetches private data outside a Route Handler or Server Action
rules.summary: The cross-stack/route-handler-session rule flags every exported HTTP method handler in a route file and every exported or inline Server Action that neither calls the configured session helper nor is wrapped by a configured wrapper, and the backend makes the authorization decision.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: no bulk suppression for a Tier-1 rule; each existing handler without the check gets a dated allowlist entry.

rules.title: Refuse cross-site, missing and null origins on mutating requests in the same-origin check

gate.id: [SEC-035] assertSameOrigin refuses cross-site, missing and null origins

rules.summary: Unit tests of the shipped assertSameOrigin helper pass only Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or an exact Origin match and expect 403 before any work for same-site, cross-site, sibling-subdomain, missing and null origins.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the helper ships with the bff-auth module; clients that strip both Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site can no longer mutate through the BFF.

rules.title: Write session cookies per the cookie contract: __Host- prefix, HttpOnly, Secure, explicit SameSite

gate.id: [SEC-036] session cookie writes match the cookie contract

evasions: a cookie written outside the session module
an ingress that lets clients set the forwarded protocol header
rules.summary: A table-driven test over the session module's set, clear and hint writers asserts every Set-Cookie attribute, including an explicit SameSite of Lax or Strict rather than the browser default, clears written as Max-Age=0 with the same attributes and a hint that holds a constant marker.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the session module ships with bff-auth; existing cookies are renamed with the migration playbook.

rules.title: Write and clear session cookies only in the session module
evasions: a cookie name assembled at runtime from unrelated fragments
rules.summary: The cross-stack/session-cookie-single-writer rule flags cookie set and delete calls that name a session cookie, and imports of the session cookie-name constants, outside the session module and its tests.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing writers go into the shrink-only ESLint bulk suppressions.

rules.title: Never hand the token to page JavaScript in the login response

gate.id: [SEC-038] the login response never contains the token

evasions: a new auth handler that relays the upstream body verbatim
rules.summary: A login route test with a mocked upstream asserts that the response JSON holds no token at any path and that Set-Cookie carries it HttpOnly.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the login handler ships with bff-auth.

rules.title: Expire every session cookie on sign-out, a failed upstream logout and a relayed 401 included

gate.id: [SEC-039] every sign-out event expires all session cookies

evasions: a second logout path that bypasses the shared clearing helper
rules.summary: Route tests with a mocked upstream assert Max-Age=0 for every token cookie and the hint after a logout that succeeds, gets a 500 or hits a network error, and after the catch-all relays a 401.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the logout handler and the catch-all ship with bff-auth.

rules.title: Keep the session-presence predicates in agreement, treating an empty cookie as signed out

gate.id: [SEC-040] session presence predicates agree on every cookie state

evasions: a new presence check written outside the shared predicates
rules.summary: One table of cookie states runs against every presence predicate, request-side and server-headers-side, which must return the same answer and treat an empty token cookie as signed out.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the predicates ship with bff-auth.

rules.title: Forward only allow-listed headers through the BFF, never Cookie, Host or a client Authorization

gate.id: [SEC-041] forwarded headers match the allow-lists in both directions

evasions: Cookie, Authorization or Set-Cookie added to an allow-list in configuration
a handler that forwards with its own fetch call
rules.summary: A forwarder test with a mocked fetch asserts that outbound headers equal the request allow-list plus the server-set Authorization and the forced JSON headers, and that relayed headers equal the response allow-list.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the forwarder ships with bff-auth.

rules.title: Keep BFF path forwarding inside the configured API base path

gate.id: [SEC-042] forwarded paths cannot escape the API base path

evasions: a handler that builds the upstream URL without the shipped builder
an encoding missing from the test table
rules.summary: The proxy builds the upstream URL from the decoded segment array, rejects empty, dot, dot-dot and slash, backslash or control-character segments, re-encodes each one and asserts origin and base-path prefix; tests for traversal, double encoding and query or fragment injection expect 400 before any fetch.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the URL builder ships with bff-auth and replaces any string-joining proxy.

rules.title: Give route files only to the catch-all, the auth routes and allowlisted handlers

gate.id: [SEC-043] the only route files are the catch-all, the auth routes and allowlisted handlers

rules.summary: A web architecture test lists every route file in the app directory and fails any that is not the catch-all proxy, an auth route or a dated allowlist entry; Server Actions are browser-invokable too and are held by SEC-034, not by this list.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing dedicated handlers get dated entries that name their reason.

rules.title: Call only the same-origin BFF from the browser, never the API origin
evasions: an absolute URL assembled from variables at runtime
an HTTP client instance created with a configurable base URL
rules.summary: The cross-stack/no-direct-api-origin rule flags absolute http(s) URL literals passed to fetch, HTTP-client factories, EventSource and WebSocket outside the configured server paths.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing direct calls go into the shrink-only ESLint bulk suppressions.

rules.title: Resolve Next.js at or above the Standard's security floor
rules.summary: The kit's floor check reads the next version resolved in the lockfile and fails below the minimum patched version kept in one data file that docs and templates also read, because audit tools can lag the framework's own advisories.
rules.adoption: Fix first: upgrade next to the floor before adopting; it is a patch-level bump within 16.x.

rules.title: Use browser storage only through the storage module, and sessionStorage never
evasions: a property name computed at runtime
a credential written under a non-credential key inside the storage module
IndexedDB or script-readable document.cookie writes
keys the storage module fails to clear at session end
rules.summary: The scope-aware cross-stack/no-web-storage rule flags the localStorage and sessionStorage globals and member access to them outside the storage module, and sessionStorage everywhere; the module's keys are typed, never hold credentials and are cleared at session end.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: no ESLint bulk suppressions for this rule; each existing use needs a dated allowlist entry linked to a migration ADR.

rules.title: Write no raw HTML sinks such as dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML or document.write
evasions: a third-party component that renders an HTML string
another HTML-parsing API such as DOMParser or Range.createContextualFragment
a property name computed at runtime
rules.summary: The cross-stack/no-raw-html rule flags the dangerouslySetInnerHTML key in JSX attributes, spread objects and createElement props, innerHTML and outerHTML assignments and insertAdjacentHTML and document.write calls; rich text renders only through one ADR-approved sanitizing wrapper.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing sinks get dated entries until they move behind the sanitizing wrapper.

rules.title: Point browser tooling only at local or dev test accounts, and copy nothing it observes
rules.summary: Because the Chrome DevTools MCP companion can see cookies and request headers, reviewers verify it is only aimed at local or development environments signed in with test accounts, and that nothing it captures leaves the machine.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt states it when it offers the companion, and it is checked in review.

rules.title: Keep auth tokens only in the OS secure store and credentials out of the storage module
rules.summary: expo-secure-store is the only credential store and the storage module's keys never hold tokens or other credentials, which reviewers confirm, because a key-name scan misses renamed keys and flags legitimate secure-store writes.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review; reviewers move any credential found in general storage behind the secure-store wrapper.

rules.title: Import unencrypted key-value stores only from the storage module
rules.summary: A dependency-cruiser rule over the resolved import graph (static, dynamic and require) lets only the storage module import @react-native-async-storage/async-storage, expo-sqlite/kv-store, expo-sqlite/localStorage/install and react-native-mmkv.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing imports go into the dependency-cruiser known-violations file (shrink-only under check-baselines), with a codemod to the storage module.

rules.title: Take device-storage keys only from the declared, app-namespaced keys module
evasions: a key passed through a variable or cast to the key type
storage reached through an alias of the storage module
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: The storage module's get, set and remove accept only the key union of the keys module, whose values match the configured app namespace, and a global no-restricted-syntax selector fails storage calls that pass a string or template literal instead of a declared key.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing literal keys go into the shrink-only ESLint bulk suppressions.

rules.title: Import the secure store only in the credential wrapper, used only by the API client and auth
evasions: the secure-store library reached through a re-export in a module the rule allows
a second secure-storage library the rule does not list
rules.summary: A dependency-cruiser rule lets only the credential wrapper import the secure-store library, and only the API client and the auth context import that wrapper; whether an allowed caller keeps the token out of state and context values is checked in review (SEC-049).
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing imports go into the dependency-cruiser known-violations file, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Send the secure-store bearer token and JSON Accept and locale headers on every API request

gate.id: [SEC-053] every request carries the bearer token, Accept and Accept-Language headers

evasions: a second HTTP client instance without the interceptor
rules.summary: A contract test shipped with the API client puts a token in the mocked secure store and asserts that a request carries Authorization: Bearer, an Accept listing application/json and application/problem+json, the active locale and no cookie credentials.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the kit's API client and its contract test ship with the mobile track, and a project keeping its own client adapts it to the contract test.

rules.title: Clear the token and call the unauthorized handler on a 401 from any call except login

gate.id: [SEC-054] a 401 outside login clears the token and calls the unauthorized handler

evasions: a second HTTP client instance without the interceptor
rules.summary: A contract test asserts that a 401 on a protected request clears the secure-store token and calls the handler once, while a 401 on the exactly matched login route does neither.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the kit's interceptor and its contract test ship with the mobile track, and a project keeping its own client adapts it to the contract test.

rules.title: Record the native token strategy in a project ADR that the manifest references
evasions: an ADR that exists but omits expiry, refresh or logout
rules.summary: With the mobile track on and the rule enabled, the configured token-strategy ADR must be an existing project decision record that covers token lifetime, refresh or re-login, revocation and reinstall behaviour, and its end-to-end verification against a live backend is checked in review.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: enable it through rules.SEC-055.enabled once the token-strategy ADR is written.

rules.title: Clear the token, the server-state cache and the push registration when the session ends
rules.summary: Sign-out and a 401 clear everything the session left behind, including the push registration that would otherwise keep delivering notifications to a signed-out device, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review against the sign-out path.

rules.title: Gitignore platform service-credential files and commit only placeholder examples
evasions: a credential file under a name missing from the pattern list
rules.summary: A check runs git ls-files and git check-ignore against a configurable list of credential file patterns (keystores, .p8 and .p12 keys, build-service and service-account JSON, platform service config) and allows only *.example placeholders.
rules.adoption: Fix first: untrack and rotate any committed credential file before adopting.

rules.title: Use client permission checks only to hide or disable UI, and authorize every action on the server
rules.summary: Web and mobile clients may hide or disable controls a user cannot use, but the backend authorizes every action, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Expire the session cookie before the backend token
rules.summary: The cookie max-age is set below the token expiration and both values are documented side by side in each app's example env file, so a user never looks signed in while every call fails.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review; adopt writes both values next to each other in the example env files.

rules.title: Choose cookie-session SPA auth without a BFF only through an ADR that confirms its constraints
evasions: an ADR recorded while one of its constraints does not hold
rules.summary: When the configured web auth variant is the stateful SPA session, the manifest must reference an existing project ADR that confirms one shared site, no custom tenant domains and no non-browser clients, the constraints under which that lighter variant is safe.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: arrives with the react-spa profile after 1.0; the ADR is written when the stateful variant is declared.

rules.title: Inject production secrets at runtime from the platform, never commit or bake them in
rules.summary: Deployments receive secrets from the platform at runtime, and no image, bundle or build artifact contains one, which reviewers confirm.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Give quality jobs no secrets, so no build or test step can need a runtime secret
evasions: a step that fetches a secret at runtime from a cloud store or file
a build step with a hardcoded fallback for a missing secret
rules.summary: A workflow check fails when a quality job, its reusable workflow or the workflow-level env references the secrets context or passes secrets: inherit, so builds, tests and the mobile bundle export run without credentials.
rules.adoption: Fix first: move secret-dependent steps out of the quality job into deploy jobs that need them.

rules.title: Commit no secret: run a pinned secret scanner over every commit range in CI
evasions: a custom secret format with no matching scanner rule and low entropy
a secret split or encoded across strings or lines
rules.summary: A CI step runs a checksum-verified, pinned gitleaks over the commit range with the project config and pre-commit runs it on staged changes, covering the source files of every track, so no separate per-track credential regex scan ships; violation fixtures use synthetic secret-shaped strings that match no real provider format.
rules.adoption: Fix first: findings in history are rotated, then recorded in the scanner's ignore file under code-owner review.

rules.title: Keep env example files to keys and placeholders, never secret values
evasions: a secret stored under a key name the patterns miss
a real value shaped like a placeholder
rules.summary: An example-file check parses every env example file in the declared track roots and fails when a key matching the configured secret-name patterns, *_KEY names included, has a value that is neither empty nor an allowed placeholder.
rules.adoption: Fix first: blank the values (and rotate any real secret) before adopting.

rules.title: Pin third-party tooling: actions to full commit SHAs, MCP servers and CLI tools to exact versions
evasions: a tool fetched by a script outside the scanned paths
a pinned tool that downloads unpinned plugins at runtime
rules.summary: A token scan of workflow uses: references (40-hex SHA required), .mcp.json and package scripts (exact versions, no @latest) and shell scripts (no clone or download of an unpinned ref) fails on any moving reference that is not allowlisted.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: adopt offers automated SHA pinning of existing tag-pinned actions, and anything left gets a dated allowlist entry rather than a hard failure.

rules.title: Import the error-tracking SDK only in the logger module
rules.summary: With the observability module, the cross-stack/module-boundary rule resolves static, dynamic, require and export-from specifiers and reports the configured SDK packages outside the logger module and the framework instrumentation files.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: arrives with the observability module after 1.0 and is turned on through rules.SEC-066.enabled.

rules.title: Call the shared same-origin check in every mutating Route Handler
evasions: the check is reached through an alias the rule does not resolve
the check is called after a side effect has already run
rules.summary: The cross-stack/same-origin-mutations rule fails every exported POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE handler in a route file that does not call the shared assertSameOrigin helper before doing any work.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: no bulk suppression for a Tier-1 rule; existing handlers get dated allowlist entries until they call the helper.

rules.title: List only exact hosts as Server Action allowed origins, never null or a wildcard
evasions: an allowedOrigins value computed at runtime
rules.summary: A config check reads experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins and fails on "null" or any entry containing *, unless a dated allowlist entry records why, because a wildcard admits sibling tenant subdomains.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: an existing wildcard entry needs a dated allowlist entry with its reason.

rules.title: Throw when a record is created with an explicit foreign tenant id

gate.id: [SEC-069] creating a record with a foreign tenant id throws

evasions: inserts through the query builder or the DB facade skip model events
saveQuietly() or withoutEvents() skip the creating hook
rules.summary: A shipped feature test has a non-platform user create a tenant-scoped record with another tenant's id and asserts that the tenant trait's creating hook throws instead of saving it.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the behaviour ships with the tenant trait and the test ships complete.

rules.title: Change nothing in GET and HEAD Route Handlers: no cookie writes, no mutating upstream calls
evasions: a mutation reached through a helper the rule does not resolve
a fetch whose method is computed at runtime
rules.summary: The cross-stack/no-mutating-get-handler rule fails exported GET and HEAD handlers in route files that set or delete cookies or call an upstream method other than GET or HEAD, because SameSite=Lax cookies ride top-level navigations.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the shrink-only ESLint bulk suppressions.

rules.title: Ship the mandated auth and authorization suites complete, with no todo, skipped or incomplete test
evasions: a mandated test whose assertions are trivially true
a skip or incomplete call made through a helper the token scan does not recognise
rules.summary: The check asserts that every mandated test of the authentication and authorization suites exists and reads PHP tokens, ignoring comments and strings, to fail on ->todo(, ->skip(, markTestIncomplete( and markTestSkipped( in those suites, with waivers only as dated allowlist entries; BE-107 owns the runner flags.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: a suite that cannot run yet needs a dated allowlist waiver; failOnSkipped stays off so environment skips elsewhere keep working.

rules.title: Export no runtime segment config from proxy.ts

gate.id: [SEC-072] the proxy exports no runtime segment config

rules.summary: A web architecture test imports the proxy module and fails when it exports runtime, because the Next.js 16 proxy runs only on the Node.js runtime and a runtime export is left over from the edge middleware model.
rules.adoption: Fix first: delete the runtime export while renaming middleware to proxy.

rules.title: Run Chrome DevTools MCP only from the pinned companion plugin, unapproved in settings
evasions: a second chrome-devtools-mcp plugin from another marketplace, or a user-scope install outside the project's settings
a project .mcp.json server of the same name next to the companion
the server approved in settings.local.json or user settings, which are not committed
rules.summary: A doctor check requires chrome-devtools-mcp to come from the Standard's pinned marketplace entry, which runs an exact version with --isolated, --no-usage-statistics, --no-performance-crux and --redact-network-headers, with no second copy beside it and no committed enabledMcpjsonServers or enableAllProjectMcpServers.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: adopt offers the companion and installs it at project scope when the user agrees; headless and CI runs disable the server.

rules.title: Ask before the browser companion opens a non-development site, runs a page script or uploads a file
evasions: a page reached from an allowed page by a link or redirect, which opens no new page through the tool
the bypassPermissions mode skips the ask decision
a browser MCP server under another name than the companion's

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: On every Chrome DevTools MCP action the PreToolUse hook asks unless the explicit URL opened, or the session's known current page, is http(s) on a local or browserHosts host; back, forward, page scripts, uploads and unknown tools always ask, and every call is denied without an explicit true in the consent record.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: development hosts beyond the built-in ones go in hooks.preToolUse.browserHosts.

rules.title: Ask before the Figma companion runs any tool that can change a Figma file
evasions: the bypassPermissions mode skips the ask decision
a Figma MCP server under another name than the companion's

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: Every Figma MCP companion tool that is not a known read (anything that can create, edit or upload to a Figma file) makes the PreToolUse hook ask the user first; reads such as get_design_context and get_metadata pass, and every call is denied when the project declined the companion.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: reading designs asks nothing.

rules.title: Take user-visible server messages from translation keys, never literal sentences
evasions: a literal sentence held in a variable or constant before it is passed
a message set inside a custom exception class
problem-detail fields assembled in an array outside the checked calls
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule requires the message arguments of abort(), Response::deny(), the response helper and problem-detail title and detail to be __() or trans() calls, so every message the API returns can be localized.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Implement HasLocalePreference on every notifiable model
rules.summary: A reflection test over app/ requires every class that uses the Notifiable trait to implement HasLocalePreference, so mail and notifications render in the recipient's stored locale rather than the request's.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries per model until its locale preference is stored.

rules.title: Set the locale before authentication, throttling and route-model binding on every API route

gate.id: [I18N-003] every api route sets the locale before auth, throttle and bindings

rules.summary: With two or more configured locales, a test resolves the HTTP kernel, gathers the global and route middleware of every api/ route (asserting the set is not empty) and fails when the locale middleware is missing or runs after authentication, throttling or SubstituteBindings, so 401, 404 and 429 messages are localized too.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit's bootstrap template prepends the locale middleware to the api group.

rules.title: Set the application locale only in the locale middleware and the locale-scoping helpers
evasions: a request value passed to setLocale() inside an allowed helper
a dynamically named method call or call_user_func
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule reports setLocale() calls outside the locale middleware and the helpers that switch the locale for a block and restore it, so no request value changes the locale without passing the configured-locale allowlist.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Keep the backend's supported-locales config equal to the manifest's locales list

gate.id: [I18N-005] supported locales config equals the manifest locales

rules.summary: A test compares the backend's single supported-locales config list with the locales in .cross-stack/standard.json and fails on any difference, so the API accepts exactly the configured locales and falls back to the default for any other.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes the config list from the manifest.

rules.title: Keep server lang files in parity across the configured locales

gate.id: [I18N-006] server lang files are in parity across locales

rules.summary: A test loads lang/<locale>/*.php and lang/<locale>.json for every configured locale and fails on a missing or extra key, an empty value, a :placeholder mismatch or a value identical to the source locale's without a dated allowlist entry.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for framework strings a brownfield locale still lacks.

rules.title: Define every statically referenced server translation key in every configured locale
evasions: keys built at run time or passed through a variable
keys resolved through a wrapper function the rule does not know
rules.summary: A custom PHPStan rule resolves literal keys passed to __(), trans(), trans_choice() and Lang::get() against the group and JSON lang files of each configured locale, so a missing key never renders as its raw name.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing findings go into the PHPStan baseline, which only shrinks.

rules.title: Translate the attribute name of every validated field in every configured locale

gate.id: [I18N-008] validation attribute names are translated for every locale

evasions: rules() that need route or user context cannot be evaluated by reflection
validation run outside FormRequests
rules.summary: A reflection test reads each FormRequest's rules() and requires an attributes() entry or a validation.attributes lang entry for every field in every configured locale, so validation messages never show raw field names.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries per FormRequest until its attribute names are translated.

rules.title: Leave no server locale plumbing behind while the i18n module is off

gate.id: [I18N-009] ships no server locale plumbing without the i18n module

evasions: locale fragments the scan does not recognise, such as per-locale branches in plain PHP
locale-suffixed columns whose suffix is outside the scanned language codes
rules.summary: When the i18n module is off, a test fails on a second locale directory under lang/, setLocale() calls or a locale middleware in app/ and bootstrap/, and *_<locale> columns in the migrated schema, so a project wires localization completely or not at all.
rules.adoption: Fix first: remove leftover locale fragments or switch the module on; a project that published only the default locale's lang files already passes.

rules.title: Have a person write or review translations, never generate them just to satisfy parity
rules.summary: Reviewers check new locale values, because the parity gate catches only missing, empty and source-identical values, not machine output or filler committed to make a check pass.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Store each model's multilingual content with one declared strategy, never a mix
rules.summary: A model uses either per-locale columns or JSON translations for all of its translatable attributes, chosen by the documented criteria, and reviewers reject a model that mixes the two.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: turned on through rules.I18N-011.enabled once the translatable-storage decision is accepted.

rules.title: Use logical-direction utility classes, never physical left and right
evasions: class names assembled at run time from fragments
stylesheets and CSS modules, including @apply, which the rule does not lint
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-physical-direction splits class strings into utilities, strips variant, important and negative prefixes and reports physical margin, padding, inset, text-align, rounding, border, float, clear and scroll utilities, plus the deprecated start and end inset names, whenever a configured locale is right-to-left.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Use logical properties in style objects, never physical left and right
evasions: style objects imported from another module
keys or values computed at run time
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-physical-direction reads inline styles, same-file style objects and React Native style sheets and reports physical side properties, shorthands, corner radii and left or right textAlign and float values whenever a configured locale is right-to-left.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Pair every physical value with its right-to-left counterpart and mirror directional icons
rules.summary: Where a value must stay physical, the same place carries its right-to-left counterpart (the rtl: variant on the web, a direction check on mobile) and a described disable comment, and elements such as back chevrons or edge slide-ins mirror with the direction.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Reference only translation keys that exist in the source locale's typed web messages
evasions: keys cast to the library's key type or to a looser type
keys built at run time where the library accepts plain strings
rules.summary: The installed i18n library's type augmentation is generated from the source locale's messages, so the type check rejects an unknown static namespace or key, and the kit's check-typed-keys sub-check fails when the augmentation is missing or out of date.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt generates the augmentation; parity gaps are handled by the parity rules.

rules.title: Put user-facing copy in message files, not JSX literals
evasions: copy held in variables, constants or objects outside JSX
props excluded by the rule's ignore list
rules.summary: react/jsx-no-literals with noStrings and a project allowlist reports JSX text and string attributes in web and mobile components, tests and fixtures excepted, so every visible string passes through the message files that parity checks.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Write no source literal in a script used only by non-source locales
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-locale-script-literal matches string, template and JSX text literals in JavaScript and TypeScript source, test files excepted, against the Unicode scripts of the configured non-source locales, presentation forms included, so right-to-left and other translated text lives only in message files.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Never choose user-facing copy by comparing the locale with a literal
evasions: lookup objects keyed by locale
string methods such as locale.startsWith()
comparisons with a variable that holds the locale literal
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-locale-branching reports conditional, logical, if and switch tests that compare a value with a configured locale literal outside the localized-field helper, so copy comes from message files rather than hard-coded locale branches.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Never render backend *_label fields as labels on a client
evasions: presentation fields named without the _label suffix
keys built at run time
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-label-field-read reports reads of properties ending in _label through dot access, literal computed keys and destructuring in web and mobile code, so enum and status labels render from the client's message files.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Make the localized-field helper prefer the reader's locale and fall back through the chain

gate.id: [I18N-020] localized-field helper follows the locale fallback chain

evasions: inputs outside the test table
a second helper the test does not import
rules.summary: A table-driven test over the configured locales asserts that the helper returns the current locale's value, then the default locale's, then the others', skipping empty values.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit ships the helper and its test.

rules.title: Prefix every locale route, never auto-detect, and use the configured locales and a project cookie

gate.id: [I18N-021] locale routing config matches the project config

evasions: a second routing configuration the test does not import
rules.summary: A test imports the routing configuration and asserts localePrefix always, localeDetection false, locales and defaultLocale equal to the project configuration and a locale cookie name other than the library default, so the URL alone decides the locale.
rules.adoption: Fix first: brownfield routing is migrated to the kit's routing module.

rules.title: Pin the configured business time zone in the i18n request configuration

gate.id: [I18N-022] i18n request config pins the configured time zone

evasions: a request configuration that does not use the exported constant
rules.summary: A test asserts that the time zone the request configuration exports is a valid IANA zone equal to the configured business time zone, so server and client render dates identically.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes the configured zone.

rules.title: Navigate only through the locale-aware wrappers, never next/link or the replaced router APIs
evasions: a third-party link or router component that wraps next/link or next/navigation internally
a replaced API reached through a namespace import of next/navigation
rules.summary: A cross-stack/module-boundary entry reports static, dynamic, require and export-from imports of next/link and of useRouter, usePathname, redirect and permanentRedirect from next/navigation outside the i18n navigation module, so every link and redirect keeps the locale prefix.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Never hand-build locale-prefixed hrefs
evasions: string concatenation
a locale variable with another name
a prefix built by a helper function
a later config object that redefines no-restricted-syntax for some files, replacing every selector there
rules.summary: A global no-restricted-syntax selector reports template literals whose text starts with a slash followed by the locale identifier anywhere in web code, because the locale-aware wrappers add the prefix, the navigation module included.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Derive the current locale from the URL in one helper that accepts only configured locales

gate.id: [I18N-025] locale-from-path helper returns only configured locales

evasions: pathname splitting outside the helper
rules.summary: A test feeds the helper every configured locale, region and script subtags included, plus unknown segments, and asserts that only configured locales are returned and anything else yields the default.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit ships the helper and its test.

rules.title: Place every page route under the locale segment

gate.id: [I18N-026] architecture: no page route outside the locale segment

rules.summary: An architecture test lists the page files under the app directory and fails on any outside the locale segment, framework root files excepted, so no screen is reachable without a locale.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for legacy pages still being moved under the locale segment.

rules.title: Set lang and dir on the document root from the active locale
evasions: lang or dir bound to an expression that does not derive from the active locale
rules.summary: cross-stack/html-lang-dir requires the root layout's html element to bind lang and dir to expressions, with the direction taken from the hard-coded right-to-left locale list, so layout and assistive technology follow the active locale.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Change layout direction and reload for a language only in the setAppLanguage() utility
evasions: computed member access on I18nManager
a wrapper in another module that the rule cannot trace
rules.summary: cross-stack/confine-api confines I18nManager.forceRTL, allowRTL and swapLeftAndRightInRTL, in member, destructured, namespace and require forms, and reload calls to the configured language utility, which persists the choice, applies the direction and reloads behind a reload-loop guard.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Declare every configured locale in supportedLocales and never set supportsRTL or forcesRTL
rules.summary: A config check evaluates the resolved app config, dynamic config files included, and fails when the expo-localization plugin's supportedLocales misses a configured locale or supportsRTL or forcesRTL is true, since on SDK 57 those static options override the in-app language choice.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes supportedLocales from the manifest.

rules.title: Reference only translation keys that exist in the source locale's typed mobile resources
evasions: keys cast to a plain string or a looser type
keys built at run time
rules.summary: The type check runs with the i18n library's typed resources generated from the source locale's messages, so an unknown static key fails compilation, and the kit's check-typed-keys sub-check fails when the typed resources are missing or out of date.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt generates the typed resources.

rules.title: Normalize locale digits in numeric input to the configured numbering system before submission
rules.summary: Clients convert Arabic-Indic and Extended Arabic-Indic digits typed into numeric fields to the configured numbering system before client validation and submission, and the backend validates the normalized value.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: turned on through rules.I18N-032.enabled once the explicit Intl formatting decision is accepted.

rules.title: Give every configured locale the source locale's keys, grouping plural forms by base key
rules.summary: The parity checker flattens each locale's message files and compares key sets with the source locale in both directions, grouping plural forms under their base key so a locale with other plural categories is not reported as missing keys.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for keys a brownfield locale still lacks.

rules.title: Leave no locale value empty or whitespace-only
rules.summary: The parity checker fails on any message value in any configured locale that is empty after trimming, because an empty string renders blank UI instead of falling back.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for values a brownfield locale still lacks.

rules.title: Allow a value identical to the source locale's only for an allowlisted key
rules.summary: The parity checker compares each non-source value with the source value after normalizing whitespace and fails on equality unless the key has a dated allowlist entry or matches a configured ignore pattern such as a placeholder-only value.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for intentional copies such as brand names and units.

rules.title: Use the same placeholders for a key in every locale, parsed with the track's message syntax
rules.summary: The parity checker parses messages as ICU on the web and as i18next interpolation on mobile, including unescaped, formatted and nesting forms, and compares placeholder names per key, using the union across plural forms and allowing count to be absent from zero, one and two forms.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for mismatches being fixed in a brownfield locale.

rules.title: Read multilingual content only through the localized-field helper, never *_<locale> keys
evasions: keys built at run time, such as template literals
wrappers that read the locale fields without the helper
rules.summary: cross-stack/localized-field-access reports dot, computed-literal, optional-chain and destructuring access to keys ending in _<locale> for the configured locales outside the helper module, with form and mutation code exempt by override because writes address each locale field on purpose.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing reads go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only; unrelated names that end in a locale suffix get dated allowlist entries.

rules.title: Show a screen's own copy for expected errors, keyed by problem type, with server detail as fallback
rules.summary: For failures a screen expects, clients render their own message-file copy selected by the RFC 9457 problem type and show the server's localized detail only when no local copy exists.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Send the active UI locale, not the browser's, as Accept-Language from the web client

gate.id: [I18N-039] sends the active locale as Accept-Language

evasions: a second HTTP client that bypasses the proxy or the shared client
rules.summary: A template test drives the BFF proxy, or the SPA API client, with a browser Accept-Language that differs from the active locale and asserts the upstream request carries the active locale, so server messages match the screen.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit's proxy and client set the header.

rules.title: Read the browser or device locale only in the language module, and never switch it automatically
evasions: server code reading the Accept-Language request header
detection libraries outside the configured catalogue
computed or globalThis access to navigator
rules.summary: cross-stack/no-locale-auto-detection reports navigator.language and navigator.languages reads, device-locale getters of the configured localization packages and browser language-detector imports outside the language module, so the URL, the per-app system language or the persisted in-app choice decides the language.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, shrink-only under check-baselines.

rules.title: Name in place any shortcut that is safe only while a locale cannot reach that screen
rules.summary: Reviewers reject a shortcut that is safe only because a product choice keeps a locale away from a screen, unless a comment where the shortcut lives names that dependency.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Match each locale's plural forms to the categories Intl.PluralRules reports for it
rules.summary: The parity checker groups plural keys by base key and requires each locale's categories to equal new Intl.PluralRules(locale).resolvedOptions().pluralCategories, applying the same comparison to ICU plural selectors on the web, so correct Arabic plurals pass and missing forms fail.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: dated entries for plural keys being completed in a brownfield locale.

rules.title: Answer in the requested configured locale, falling back to the default for an unlisted one

gate.id: [I18N-043] api messages follow the requested locale and fall back for an unlisted one

evasions: endpoints the test does not exercise
messages built without the translator
rules.summary: A feature test sends a request that fails validation with each configured Accept-Language and with an unlisted one and asserts the message language and the fallback, so the locale middleware is proven to work and not merely registered.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit ships the test against its own validation route.

rules.title: Derive every configured locale's direction from the one hard-coded right-to-left locale list

gate.id: [I18N-044] every configured locale gets its direction from the right-to-left locale list

evasions: direction computed elsewhere without the shared helper
rules.summary: A unit test derives the direction of every configured locale, region and script subtags included, from the shared right-to-left locale list and asserts the result, because Intl.Locale getTextInfo() is missing on Node.js 22 and in some supported browsers.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the kit ships the list, the helper and the test.

rules.title: Import no feature code or generated contract types in UI primitives
rules.summary: No module in the UI primitive folder imports, directly or transitively, from a feature folder or from the generated API contract, so primitives stay reusable and free of domain shapes.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing edges go into the dependency-cruiser known-violations baseline, which PROC-027 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Keep UI primitives from reaching the i18n library, directly or through other modules
rules.summary: No module in the UI primitive folder imports the configured i18n library, any of its subpaths or a project module that reaches it, which keeps translation in the calling feature and passes user-facing strings to primitives as props.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing edges go into the dependency-cruiser known-violations baseline, which PROC-027 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Use design tokens, never raw color literals
evasions: a color assembled from string fragments at run time
a numeric color such as 0xffffff
a raw color in a CSS file outside the token source, which ESLint does not lint
rules.summary: Class strings, style objects, SVG props and string literals in web and mobile source name colors only through design tokens, with no hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), color() or named color values outside the configured token source.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Use the z-index token ladder, never arbitrary z-index values
evasions: a z-index declared in a CSS file
a class string assembled at run time
rules.summary: Stacking order comes only from the z-index token ladder: arbitrary z-[n] classes, [z-index:n] properties, numeric z utilities the theme has removed and numeric zIndex style values are rejected.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Style with one system: no preprocessor stylesheets, CSS-in-JS modules or <style jsx> blocks
evasions: a CSS-in-JS library missing from the rule's banned list
a module loaded through a computed dynamic import specifier
styles injected at run time through a created style element
rules.summary: Source files import no .scss, .sass, .less or .styl stylesheet and no CSS-in-JS module outside the styling system declared in the stack table, and render no <style jsx> block, which Next.js supports with no dependency to detect; a competing styling library in the manifest is PROC-007's concern.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing preprocessor or CSS-in-JS imports go into ESLint bulk suppressions (shrink-only) while a declared stack migration removes them.

rules.title: Hand-write CSS only where the utility system falls short, each block with a why-comment
evasions: a boilerplate comment that names no limitation
a CSS file outside the configured globs
styling written as inline style objects instead of CSS
rules.summary: Every rule block in project CSS outside the token source is preceded by a comment that names what the installed utility system could not express, so hand-written CSS stays the documented escape hatch.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: existing uncommented blocks go into a dated allowlist file that shrinks as blocks are commented or removed.

rules.title: Define design tokens in one source; other CSS may only alias them
evasions: a CSS file outside the configured globs
a custom property set in an inline style object or an arbitrary-property class
rules.summary: Custom properties declared outside the token source's theme block are pure var() aliases of theme tokens, so every design value has a single definition.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: existing declarations outside the token source get dated entries and move into the source over time.

rules.title: Compose chart and SVG color token references only in the chart-token module
evasions: a token reference assembled from string fragments
a token value read at run time through getComputedStyle
rules.summary: String and template literals containing var(--color-...) appear only in the configured chart-token module, so charts and SVGs take their colors from one token mapping.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Reference color tokens without fallback values
evasions: a fallback written in a CSS file
a fallback assembled from string fragments
rules.summary: A var(--token) reference in string or template literals carries no fallback value, so a missing token fails visibly instead of silently rendering a hard-coded color.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Route overlays through the shared overlay utilities; no createPortal elsewhere
evasions: a portal component from a third-party UI library
per-component focus-trap or positioning code that needs no portal
rules.summary: A cross-stack/confine-api entry lets only the configured overlay modules reach createPortal from react-dom, whether imported by name, through the default or a namespace import or through require, so dialogs, popovers and menus share one focus-trap, positioning and z-index path.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: existing portals go into ESLint bulk suppressions until they move behind the overlay utilities.

rules.title: Render loading, error and empty states through the shared state primitives
rules.summary: Web and mobile screens show loading, error and empty states through the shared skeleton, error-state and empty-state primitives rather than hand-rolled per-page blocks, so request states look and behave the same everywhere.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review as screens are touched.

rules.title: Pass an automated accessibility scan, target size included, on every journey page
evasions: states and screens the journey never renders
axe rules or selectors excluded in the scan configuration
defects automated scanning cannot detect, such as an inaccurate accessible name
rules.summary: A local accessibility command, which the end-to-end CI step only calls, scans every page the journey visits plus a UI-primitives fixture page with the WCAG 2.2 AA axe tags, target size included, and fails on any violation.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: turned on with the end-to-end job; each known violation gets a dated allowlist entry with a reason.

rules.title: Browser-check every changed screen before reporting UI work done
rules.summary: With the browser-check module on, each changed screen is opened with the Chrome DevTools MCP companion against a local or development environment and checked for rendering, console errors and failed requests before UI work is reported done.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: applies to new UI work once the companion is installed and the module is on.

rules.title: Reference the platform Text and TextInput components only inside the text primitives
evasions: a third-party component that renders platform text internally
a text component re-exported by a module outside the configured extra sources
rules.summary: React Native Text and TextInput, in named, namespace, default-member and require forms, through Animated.Text and Animated.createAnimatedComponent(TextInput), plus TextInput from configured extra sources, are referenced only in the configured primitive files, so all text renders through the text primitives.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Take spacing, sizes, radii and font sizes from tokens, not numeric literals
evasions: a number routed through a local constant
a value computed from variables
rules.summary: Numeric literals on the configured spacing, size, radius and typography keys inside mobile style objects are rejected except a small allowed set such as 0 and 1, so layout values come from the token scale.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: existing literals go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Define styles through the theme style factory
evasions: a plain style object passed straight to a style prop
styles built in a helper outside the factory
StyleSheet.create reached through an alias or computed member access
rules.summary: StyleSheet.create from react-native is called only in the configured style-factory module, so every screen builds its styles from theme tokens through one factory.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: existing StyleSheet.create calls go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Type light and dark palettes with one shared interface so their keys cannot drift
evasions: a palette declared outside the configured token module
an as-cast or an any-typed value inside a palette
optional keys in the shared interface
rules.summary: Each palette in the gate-protected color-token module is declared with satisfies against one shared palette interface, which the kit's check-typed-keys sub-check asserts, so a missing or extra key fails the type check.
rules.adoption: Fix first: an existing palette file adds the satisfies annotation once; the kit's token module ships with it.

rules.title: Map domain states to color tokens in one per-domain module, never inline
rules.summary: The client maps each semantic state the API emits to a color token in one module per domain, and screens import that mapping rather than choosing colors inline.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review as screens are touched.

rules.title: Declare an accessibility role on every touchable
evasions: a touchable component missing from the configured list
a role value that misdescribes the control
rules.summary: Every element on the configured touchable list, including Pressable, the Touchable components, gesture-handler buttons and registered wrappers, carries accessibilityRole or role, and a prop spread passes only for a registered wrapper that sets the role.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing violations go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Label icon-only controls, expose selected and disabled state, and meet the minimum touch target
rules.summary: Icon-only controls carry an accessibility label, selectable and disabled controls expose their state to assistive technology, and touch targets meet the minimum touch-target size token.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review as controls are touched.

rules.title: Run impeccable's audit, critique and polish commands on UI changes before calling them done
rules.summary: With the design module on, UI changes go through the impeccable companion's audit, critique and polish commands against the project's own design tokens before they are reported done, and its new-work or redesign modes are never run on an existing product.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: applies to new UI work once the companion is installed and the module is on.

rules.title: Install impeccable only from the pinned companion plugin, without its hooks
evasions: impeccable installed from another marketplace or copied into the skills directory, outside the Standard's marketplace entry
the engine binary, which the plugin commit does not pin, replaced after its first download
only the committed settings are checked where impeccable is not installed, such as in CI
rules.summary: With the design module on, doctor checks that impeccable comes from the Standard's marketplace entry, pinned to a commit and loading its skill and agents without its hooks, that no second copy is installed or copied in beside it, and reports the engine download and the update-check and telemetry switches.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: adopt offers the companion and installs it at project scope when the user agrees.

rules.title: Declare tracks, tier and modules in a schema-valid manifest that covers every detected stack
rules.summary: The project records its tracks, tier, modules and locales in .cross-stack/standard.json, which validates against the published schema and names a track root under trackRoots for every Laravel, web or mobile manifest in the repository.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes the manifest with a track root for every detected manifest, so the check passes from the first run.

rules.title: Declare Tier 2 when at least two tier triggers hold, or record why it is declined
evasions: tier triggers declared falsely in the manifest
a boilerplate decline reason
rules.summary: When at least two of the declared tier triggers hold (multi-tenant, more than one developer, long-lived; multi-tenant is implied by the tenancy module), the manifest declares tier 2 or references, under decisions, the project decision record that gives the reason for staying at tier 1.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt asks for the triggers and records tier 2, or writes the decision record that declines it and references it from the manifest.

rules.title: Install each declared track and module as a complete unit, and leave no substrate of the others
evasions: a required file present but hollowed out
a registration present but unreachable at run time
rules.summary: doctor checks, for every declared track and module, the version's list of required gate files, plumbing, registrations, tests and path-scoped rule files, and reports substrate left behind by a module that is switched off.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt installs each declared track and module as a unit; doctor reports leftovers of an undeclared module for removal.

rules.title: Enable the Standard's plugin in the repository's committed .claude/settings.json
evasions: the committed value is overridden to false in settings.local.json or user settings
managed settings disable the plugin for the machine
rules.summary: The committed .claude/settings.json lists the Standard's marketplace in extraKnownMarketplaces and sets the plugin to true in enabledPlugins, so every contributor's session loads the same skills and hooks.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt merges the two entries into an existing .claude/settings.json without touching its other keys.

rules.title: Record the stack table in the manifest, every concern filled and every named package installed
evasions: the table is accurate but new code ignores it
a concern missing from the configured concern list
rules.summary: The manifest's stack section names the installed library for each configured concern, every named package resolves in the track's package.json or composer.json, and a concern marked none states how it is met instead.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt pre-fills the table from the installed manifests for the team to review.

rules.title: Prefer the installed library's idiomatic API, then its escape hatch, and explain hand-written code
rules.summary: For each concern the installed library's idiomatic API comes first and its documented escape hatch second, hand-written code carries a comment naming what the library could not express, and an outdated version is upgraded instead of worked around.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Install at most one library per concern, test runners included
evasions: a library outside the curated concern catalogue
a vendored copy or a hand-written equivalent of a second library
a tool run through npx or a global install with no manifest entry
rules.summary: Each concern (state, server state, forms, validation, HTTP, dates, styling, unit tests, end-to-end tests) has one installed library unless a declared migration names the winner and the deprecated loser, and the Standard's own gate tooling is exempt.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing competing pairs are declared as a migration with a winner and a deprecated loser, which PROC-008 then confines, and the Standard's own enforcement tools are pre-exempted.

rules.title: Import a deprecated library only inside its declared legacy paths, so new code uses the winner
evasions: a module inside the declared legacy paths that re-exports the deprecated library to new code
rules.summary: In web and mobile source, a static, dynamic, require or export-from import of a package declared deprecated for a concern is reported outside that concern's declared legacy paths, so the migration to the winner only moves forward.
rules.adoption: Baseline: the deprecated library's current import sites are declared as its legacy paths, so only new imports fail.

rules.title: Land each new runtime dependency with an ADR that names the alternatives considered
evasions: a boilerplate decision record that names no real alternatives
code vendored into the repository instead of added as a dependency
runtime code importing a package declared only as a development dependency
rules.summary: Each package added to the production dependencies of a package.json or composer.json, compared with the base branch, is named in a decision record added or changed in the same change, and that record lists the alternatives considered.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: only dependencies added after adoption are checked, because the check compares with the base branch.

rules.title: Keep business rules on the backend, and name and test the source of any deliberate client mirror
rules.summary: Business rules live on the server, client validation is user-experience feedback while the server decides validity, and a deliberate client mirror of a rule names its backend source and has a test that compares the two.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Keep copied gate files equal to the adopted templates, except inside declared configuration regions
evasions: a weakening made inside a declared configuration region
an extra project config file the template manifest does not list that overrides a kit setting
rules.summary: doctor hashes each kit-copied gate file, security plumbing included, outside its declared configuration regions and compares the hash and version header with the template manifest of the version recorded in .cross-stack/standard.json, so a locally weakened copy is reported.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt records the adopted version, so only later edits outside the configuration regions are reported.

rules.title: Never delete or weaken a gate to get green; fix the code, record a dated exception or a waiver
rules.summary: A red gate is answered by fixing the code, by a dated allowlist or shrink-only baseline entry, or by a waiver recorded in a decision record, never by deleting the gate, lowering its level or turning its rule off.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Ask the user before an agent edits gate files, baselines, allowlists or CI workflows
evasions: a write through a tool, generated script or indirect command the matcher does not recognise
the bypassPermissions mode skips the ask decision

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: Before an agent edits a gate configuration, baseline, allowlist or CI workflow, or adds the opt-out line, the PreToolUse hook asks the user, and the edit goes ahead only with that approval; shell commands that bypass a gate are PROC-026's.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt also writes permissions.ask rules for gate configurations and permissions.deny rules for baselines and allowlists into .claude/settings.json, which hold in every permission mode.

rules.title: Give every allowlist entry a reason and an expiry date, and fail CI once the date has passed
rules.summary: Entries in .cross-stack/allowlists/ validate against a schema that requires a non-empty reason and an ISO expiry date no further ahead than allowlistMaxDays, and the check fails once an entry's expiry date has passed.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: adopt writes an entry with a reason and an expiry date inside allowlistMaxDays for each existing exception that a gate without a native baseline reports.

rules.title: Never let the ESLint bulk-suppressions file grow
evasions: a change pushed without a pull request, where no base-branch comparison runs
ESLint run outside the checked scripts with another suppressions location
rules.summary: No file and rule pair in the committed ESLint bulk-suppressions file gains suppressions and no new pair appears compared with the base branch in pull-request CI, and every lint script uses the committed suppressions file rather than --suppressions-location elsewhere, so recorded lint debt only shrinks.
rules.adoption: Baseline: adopt sets the kit rules to error before running eslint --suppress-all, so existing violations become the starting suppressions and no warning is left outside the baseline.

rules.title: Describe the reason in every ESLint disable directive
rules.summary: Every eslint-disable, eslint-disable-line and eslint-disable-next-line comment ends with a -- description giving its reason, so each inline exception explains itself in review.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing directives without a description go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Trust a gate only after seeing it fail on a minimal violation and pass on clean code
rules.summary: A gate is trusted only after it has been seen failing on a minimal violation and passing on clean code, and a new or changed gate is shown failing before any change relies on it.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Keep every enabled gate with a shipped probe failing on that probe after adopting or upgrading
evasions: project ignore globs that exclude real code but not the probe location
the scheduled workflow is disabled or stops running, so probes run only when upgrading
rules.summary: doctor --probe copies each enabled rule's shipped violation probe, generated from a subset of the rule fixtures, into a scratch copy of the project, runs the rule's gate and requires a failure that names the rule, so a probed gate that was wired wrongly or silently disabled is found.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the probes run in the upgrade skill and a scheduled workflow, never as a required check on every pull request.

rules.title: Keep a numbered ADR log in the configured decisions directory in a Tier-2 project
evasions: decisions made without a record
a record that parses but states no real alternatives
rules.summary: When the manifest declares tier 2, the configured decisions directory exists and every record in it parses as MADR with a number, a status and a date.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt creates the decisions directory with a first record when tier 2 is declared.

rules.title: Name in each pull request the rule IDs or ADRs its change follows
evasions: citing a rule or decision record unrelated to the change
a change merged without a pull request
rules.summary: The pull request body cites at least one rule ID that exists in the registry or one decision record of the project, so reviewers can check the change against what it claims to follow.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: a team turns it on through rules.PROC-020.enabled once its pull request template asks for rule IDs.

rules.title: Before claiming done, re-read the diff, run the checks and report their real output verbatim
rules.summary: Before reporting work as done, the agent re-reads its diff, runs the project's check scripts and pastes their real output verbatim, and never claims that a check it did not run has passed.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Pass the fast gate before an agent session ends
evasions: the stop gate is turned off in the project config or with CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_STOP_GATE=0
a check that runs past the time budget fails open
the loop guard lets the next stop through when nothing changed since a blocked one
a project without a manifest or a check:fast script is skipped
a script whose tool (npm, Composer or PHP) is not installed is skipped with a notice

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: When an agent finishes a turn, the project's fast check runs within a time budget, and a failure blocks the stop with the failing command and the end of its output.
rules.adoption: Baseline: adopt makes check:fast green through shrink-only baselines and dated allowlist entries before the Stop gate runs, and a project that cannot yet sets hooks.stop.enabled to false.

rules.title: Extract convenience duplication at the third copy, and inline any one-caller abstraction
rules.summary: Convenience duplication is extracted only at its third copy, and an abstraction with a single caller, an Action included, is treated as a defect to inline.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Extract a duplicated business rule at its second copy, including one rendered on two surfaces
rules.summary: A duplicated business rule is extracted at its second copy, including a rule rendered on two surfaces such as web and PDF or web and native, so the copies cannot drift.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review.

rules.title: Allow inline ESLint exceptions only as eslint-disable-next-line comments
rules.summary: The eslint-comments no-use rule allows only eslint-disable-next-line directives, so file-wide, block and same-line disables and inline rule configuration fail lint; PROC-031 covers naming the disabled rules and unused directives.
rules.adoption: Baseline: existing block and same-line disables go into ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Ask the user before an agent runs a shell command that skips or weakens a gate
evasions: a command form the patterns do not recognise, such as one built inside a script file or passed through an alias
the bypassPermissions mode skips the ask decision
a command run in the developer's own terminal, outside Claude Code

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: Before an agent runs a shell command that skips or weakens a gate, such as --no-verify, git commit -n, a lefthook-disabling variable, an audit or test-runner override, a baseline deleted or regenerated outside its baseline:update script, a write onto a protected file or an appended opt-out line, the user is asked and the command runs only with that approval.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the sanctioned baseline:update scripts, which regenerate a baseline and fail when it grows, are not inspected, so routine baseline maintenance asks nothing.

rules.title: Never let the dependency-cruiser known-violations baseline grow
evasions: a change pushed without a pull request, where no base-branch comparison runs
dependency-cruiser run outside the checked scripts with another known-violations file
rules.summary: The committed dependency-cruiser known-violations file gains no entry compared with the base branch in pull-request CI, and every depcruise invocation in the check scripts reads that file through --ignore-known, so a fixed violation stays fixed and a new one cannot be recorded as known.
rules.adoption: Baseline: adopt writes the current violations to the known-violations file, which becomes the starting point that can only shrink.

rules.title: Ask in the pull request template for the rule IDs a change follows and the real check output
evasions: the sections are left empty or filled with output no real run produced
a pull request opened through the API or a CLI without the template body
rules.summary: A doctor check requires the repository's pull request template to hold a section for the rule IDs or ADRs a change follows, a section for pasting the real output of the project's check and a checkbox confirming that the output is real and current.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt copies the kit template, or merges the sections into an existing pull request template.

rules.title: Keep the managed CLAUDE.md block, with any imported AGENTS.md, under 200 lines
evasions: project text outside the managed block, or in other files that CLAUDE.md imports, is not counted
CLAUDE.local.md and user-level memory files add always-loaded text the check cannot see
rules.summary: The block between the cross-stack-standard begin and end markers, together with any AGENTS.md that CLAUDE.md imports, stays under 200 lines, so the always-loaded context stays small and track detail lives in path-scoped rule files.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt merges the block into existing CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files; a project whose AGENTS.md is long moves detail into path-scoped rule files.

rules.title: Report lint errors in a file back to the agent right after it edits the file
evasions: the hook cannot undo or block the edit, so reported errors remain until the agent fixes them or the Stop gate runs
a formatter or linter that is not installed is skipped silently
a linter that crashes or rejects its configuration leaves a notice for the user instead of feedback
a run past the time budget fails open
a file changed through a shell command rather than an edit tool is not checked
PHP files get lint feedback only when hooks.postToolUse.phpstan is true

the project opts out or switches the hooks off (the opt-out line, "disabled": true in the manifest, CROSS_STACK_STANDARD_DISABLE, or the plugin disabled in Claude Code settings), or Node.js is missing, so no hook runs
rules.summary: After an agent edits or writes a file, the project's installed formatter formats it and file-scoped ESLint runs from the track root within a time budget, and lint errors go back to the agent as file:line rule message lines, so they are fixed while the file is still in context.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the hook only reports, and a project without a formatter or ESLint installed is skipped.

rules.title: Name the disabled rules in every ESLint directive and fail unused directives
evasions: a later config object that turns either setting off for files outside the sample files the check resolves
rules.summary: A config check resolves the ESLint configuration for a sample file on each JavaScript track and fails unless @eslint-community/eslint-comments/no-unlimited-disable is at error and linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives is "error", so a directive names its rules and a stale one fails lint.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt removes unused directives with eslint --fix and records existing unlimited disables as ESLint bulk suppressions, which PROC-015 keeps shrink-only.

rules.title: Keep ESLint, TypeScript, @types/node and Node inside the Standard's supported ranges
rules.summary: The kit's doctor check, run in each JavaScript track's check chain, reads the resolved eslint, typescript and @types/node versions and the engines field and fails outside the supported ranges, such as TypeScript 7 or later, under which typed lint rules and dependency-cruiser stop checking without failing.
rules.adoption: Fix first: a project outside the ranges pins the supported versions, which adopt proposes, before the check is enabled.

rules.title: Run dependency-cruiser only through the kit wrapper that fails when nothing was cruised
evasions: a check member that calls depcruise directly instead of through the wrapper
