rules.summary: The kit's check-depcruise wrapper runs dependency-cruiser with JSON output and fails when summary.totalCruised is 0 or summary.error is above 0, because an unsupported TypeScript version or a wrong path makes dependency-cruiser pass silently and its exit status wraps at 256.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt points the boundaries member of each JavaScript check chain at the wrapper.

rules.title: Never let the jscpd duplication baseline grow
evasions: a change pushed without a pull request, where no base-branch comparison runs
jscpd run outside the checked scripts with another --baseline file
rules.summary: The committed jscpd baseline gains no clone compared with the base branch in pull-request CI, every jscpd invocation in the check scripts reads that baseline, and the sanctioned baseline:update script fails on growth, so recorded duplication only shrinks.
rules.adoption: Baseline: adopt records the existing clones in the committed baseline, which becomes the starting point that can only shrink.

rules.title: Run format, analysis, tests with the coverage floor and baseline growth in the Laravel chain
evasions: a member script redefined as a no-op or with its failure swallowed, for example by appending || true
a member run with weakened flags, such as a narrowed path list
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check reads composer.json and requires the check script to run pint --test, Larastan, the Pest suite with its coverage floor and the baseline-growth check, plus a check:fast script for the Stop hook, while dependency audits stay out of both because they need the network.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes check and check:fast into composer.json and keeps any stricter existing member; doctor reports a missing PCOV or Xdebug coverage driver.

rules.title: Run typecheck, lint, format, boundaries, dead code and tests with coverage in the web chain
evasions: a member script redefined as a no-op or with its failure swallowed, for example by appending || true
a member run with weakened flags, such as a narrowed file list
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check reads package.json and requires the check script to run the typecheck, ESLint, the formatter check, dependency-cruiser, knip and the test suite with its coverage thresholds, plus a check:fast script for the Stop hook.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes check and check:fast into package.json and keeps any stricter existing member.

rules.title: Run the production build in the web quality job
evasions: the build step runs a different command under the build step's name
an if: condition skips the build step
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check requires the web quality job, or the reusable web workflow it calls, to have a step that runs the framework's production build without continue-on-error, so errors only a build reveals fail the pull request instead of a later deploy.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the reusable web workflow ships the build step; a build that needs a runtime secret is fixed before adopting.

rules.title: Run typecheck, lint, structure, format, boundaries, dead code and covered tests in the mobile chain
evasions: a member script redefined as a no-op or with its failure swallowed, for example by appending || true
a member run with weakened flags, such as a narrowed file list
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check reads package.json and requires the check script to run the typecheck, ESLint, the structure rules, the formatter check, dependency-cruiser, knip and the test suite with its coverage thresholds, plus a check:fast script for the Stop hook.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes check and check:fast into package.json, renaming an existing aggregate script rather than keeping two.

rules.title: Bundle the app with expo export in the mobile quality job
evasions: the export step runs a different command under the export step's name
an if: condition skips the export step
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check requires the mobile quality job, or the reusable mobile workflow it calls, to have a step that runs npx expo export for iOS and Android without continue-on-error, so Metro resolution and transform errors that typecheck and tests miss fail the pull request.
rules.adoption: Fix first: the reusable mobile workflow ships the export step; the bundle must build in mock mode without secrets.

rules.title: Regenerate the client API types from the exported contract in CI and fail on any diff
evasions: an if: condition skips the drift step
continue-on-error: true on the drift step
rules.summary: With the api-contract module on in a repository holding backend and client, a CI step runs one local command that exports the document with scramble:export --fail-on-unknown, regenerates the committed client types with the configured generator and fails when git diff --exit-code finds a difference.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the first generated types are committed at adoption, before the step is enabled.

rules.title: Pin the backend's published OpenAPI artifact in a standalone client and fail CI on type drift
evasions: a pin left on a stale artifact version passes until someone moves it
an artifact published without the backend's own export check
rules.summary: With the api-contract module on in a client-only repository, a CI step runs one local command that fetches the pinned version of the backend's published document, regenerates the committed types and fails on git diff --exit-code.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the pin starts at the backend's currently published version and the regenerated types are committed at adoption.

rules.title: Audit production dependencies for known vulnerabilities in every quality job
evasions: the threshold lowered through package-manager configuration the check does not read, such as an audit level in .npmrc
a finding silenced through the package manager's own ignore settings instead of a dated exception
rules.summary: A workflow check requires each declared track's quality job to run a blocking production-only audit at high severity (composer audit --locked --no-dev, npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high or the lockfile's equivalent) without continue-on-error, in CI only because audits need the network.
rules.adoption: Allowlist: a finding that cannot be fixed yet becomes a dated, reasoned exception, never a lowered threshold.

rules.title: Run every member of each track's check script as its own named CI step
evasions: a step runs a different command under a member's name
an if: condition skips a member's step
rules.summary: A CI-parity sub-check splits each track's check script into its members and requires a quality-job step running each one without continue-on-error, or a call to the Standard's reusable track workflow, so local and CI runs stay identical and a failure names its member.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt replaces hand-listed quality steps with a thin caller of the reusable track workflow.

rules.title: Run ESLint at zero warnings in every JavaScript check chain
evasions: ESLint called through a wrapper script or binary name the token check does not recognise
a warning-level rule switched off in the project config instead of fixed
rules.summary: A token check requires every ESLint invocation in the JavaScript check scripts to pass --max-warnings=0 and the mobile chain to call ESLint directly rather than expo lint, so warnings cannot pile up unseen.
rules.adoption: Baseline: bulk suppressions record errors, not warnings, so adopt sets the kit's rules to error before recording existing findings in the shrink-only suppressions file.

rules.title: Make every build, deploy or release job depend on the quality job
evasions: a deployment triggered outside the repository's workflows, such as a hosting platform's git integration
a deploy job named outside the configured pattern
rules.summary: A workflow check requires every job whose name matches the build, deploy or release pattern to reach the quality job through needs:, or to run only on a successful workflow_run of the quality workflow, so nothing ships without a green quality run.
rules.adoption: Fix first: existing build, deploy and release jobs gain needs: on the quality job; deployment itself stays out of scope.

rules.title: Reuse one quality workflow per track instead of copying its steps
evasions: a copied job edited so its step list no longer matches the reusable workflow
rules.summary: A workflow check fails when a track's check-member step sequence is defined in more than one job instead of being called through workflow_call, so a fix to the quality job cannot miss a copy.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt replaces copied quality jobs with thin callers of the reusable track workflow.

rules.title: Protect the default branch and require the quality check before merge
rules.summary: The default branch requires a pull request, lists the reusable workflow's quality check as a required status check and blocks force pushes and deletion; this is a repository setting, so reviewers confirm it.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: checked in review; a repository setting the organization applies.

rules.title: Assign a CODEOWNERS owner to every gate file, allowlist and workflow
evasions: the code owner is the author of the change
no branch rule or ruleset requires code-owner review, so ownership never blocks a merge
rules.summary: A doctor check parses CODEOWNERS and requires every protected-path glob, the built-in list plus hooks.preToolUse.protect, to match an owned entry, so gate changes have a human reviewer behind the gate-file guard.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt generates CODEOWNERS entries from the protected-path list and merges them into an existing file.

rules.title: Run the secret scan, formatters and linters on staged files before each commit
evasions: --no-verify or LEFTHOOK=0 skips the hooks
a clone where npm install never ran has no hooks installed
a lefthook-local override removes a job
rules.summary: A doctor check parses the lefthook configuration and requires pre-commit jobs on staged files for the pinned gitleaks scan and for each declared track's formatter and linter, with the hooks installed and core.hooksPath unset.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt migrates an existing husky or core.hooksPath setup into lefthook and never leaves two hook managers installed.

rules.title: Check in CI that commit messages and pull request titles follow Conventional Commits
evasions: the squash commit message edited in the merge dialog after the check ran
a direct push to a branch that requires no pull request
rules.summary: A CI step runs commitlint with the conventional config over the pull request's commit range and its title, which the workflow reads through env: rather than interpolating it into the script.
rules.adoption: Opt-in: only pull requests opened after it is turned on through rules.CI-016.enabled are linted; earlier history is left as it is.

rules.title: Publish a backend-only repository's OpenAPI document as a versioned artifact after its export
evasions: info.version left unchanged when the document changes, so two different documents share one artifact name
an artifact retention period shorter than the time standalone clients take to pin a version
rules.summary: With the api-contract module on and no client track in the repository, a workflow check asserts that an upload step follows the export step in the reusable Laravel workflow and that the artifact name carries the document's info.version, so standalone clients can pin a version.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: the reusable Laravel workflow ships the upload step after the export step.

rules.title: Delay dependency releases, group framework updates without automerge and hold risky majors
evasions: the update bot is not installed, or its pull requests are ignored
a person bumps a held package by hand
rules.summary: A doctor check reads the Renovate or Dependabot configuration and requires a release-age delay, a group for next, laravel/framework and expo without automerge, holds on the TypeScript, ESLint and mobile Jest majors and, on the mobile track, SDK-locked packages kept out of regular updates.
rules.adoption: Nothing needed: adopt writes the Renovate template, or checks an existing Dependabot configuration for the same delay, groups and holds.
